source_snapshot.title: RTA organises Dubai International Electric Vehicle Exhibition and Conference 2026
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 4th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) will organise the inaugural Dubai International Electric Vehicle Exhibition and Conference 2026 (EV World 2026) from 10th to 12th November 2026 at Dubai World Trade Centre, under the theme: Driving a Smart and Sustainable Mobility Future.The event forms part of Dubai’s vision to accelerate the shift towards a smarter, more sustainable transport system and consolidate the emirate’s position as a global hub for mobility innovation. It also reflects RTA’s commitment to accelerating the adoption of green mobility solutions, anticipating future mobility trends, and harnessing advanced technologies to develop an integrated transport system that supports sustainability and emissions-reduction goals.Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors, Roads and Transport Authority, said, “The inaugural Dubai International Electric Vehicle Exhibition and Conference 2026 (EV World 2026) reaffirms Dubai’s standing as a global hub for innovation and the future economy, and as a platform that brings together companies, investors, developers and decision-makers to chart the future of a sector experiencing rapid growth and fundamental shifts in technology, business models and value chains.”Al Tayer added, “The global public transport sector is undergoing a rapid transition towards electric and new energy vehicles, driven by major advances in battery technology, clean energy, charging infrastructure, artificial intelligence and autonomous systems. This transformation is creating significant economic and investment opportunities for cities capable of building an integrated ecosystem that combines flexible regulatory frameworks, advanced infrastructure, innovation and public-private partnerships.“Dubai has strong competitive advantages that position it to play a pivotal role in this transition, supported by an environment that attracts investment, talent and global companies, as well as a strong capacity to adopt future technologies and translate them into real-world applications. RTA has adopted the ‘Zero-Emissions Public Transportation in Dubai 2050’ strategy, becoming the first entity in the Middle East to establish a long-term strategy for transitioning to net-zero-emission public transport by 2050.”Al Tayer continued, “EV World 2026 will serve as an international platform for exchanging expertise, forging partnerships and showcasing the latest innovations in electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles, charging and sustainable energy technologies, smart infrastructure, air mobility and autonomous systems. The participation of more than 300 local and international companies, authorities and organisations reflects growing interest in Dubai as a promising market and a hub for developing future mobility solutions.”He added, “Through this event, we aim to deepen collaboration with leading global companies, research and development centres, and specialised institutions; attract advanced technologies and high-value investments; and support the development of an integrated economic ecosystem for electric and smart mobility. This will help reduce emissions, enhance the efficiency and sustainability of the transport system, support Dubai’s goals of building a more competitive and sustainable economy, and improve quality of life for current and future generations.”The event is expected to attract more than 300 local and international companies, authorities and organisations, over 30 business partners, and 70 speakers from organisations specialising in sustainable transport, along with more than 10,000 industry specialists and interested visitors.Participants will showcase the latest solutions and technologies in electric vehicle manufacturing and operations, battery management, hydrogen fuel cells, sustainable energy technologies, fast-charging stations, smart infrastructure, unmanned aerial vehicles and autonomous systems, as well as digital solutions and artificial intelligence applications that enhance the efficiency of future mobility systems.Preparations for the event are gathering pace in collaboration with local and international partners, as efforts continue to deliver an inaugural edition that reflects Dubai’s position as a global hub for innovation and advanced technologies in transport and mobility.Al Tayer met with Dr. Zhang Yongwei, Chairman of China EV100, to explore opportunities for cooperation and expand international partnerships in electric vehicles, new energy vehicles, and smart and sustainable mobility.The meeting explored ways to deepen cooperation in support of the Dubai International Electric Vehicle Exhibition and Conference 2026 and strengthen its role as a regional platform connecting government entities, global companies and leaders across the mobility sector.The two sides also discussed opportunities to exchange expertise in electric vehicles and smart and sustainable mobility, and to forge strategic partnerships with leading Chinese institutions and companies across the new energy vehicle ecosystem and future transport technologies.Preparations for the event also included the signing of a cooperation agreement with China EV100, China’s electric vehicle alliance, aimed at expanding the participation of Chinese companies and institutions in the exhibition and conference, strengthening cooperation in industry, technology, and research and development, and connecting China’s advanced capabilities with the growing investment and commercial opportunities across the UAE and the wider region.The Organising Committee also conducted a series of promotional visits and international meetings in China, Germany, Belgium and India to raise awareness of the event, attract specialised companies and institutions, expand its network of international partners, and broaden the participation of key players across electric vehicles, batteries, charging infrastructure, clean energy and smart technologies.Building on this strong local and international momentum, the Dubai International Electric Vehicle Exhibition and Conference 2026 is reinforcing its role as a leading platform bringing together stakeholders from across the electric mobility ecosystem, from manufacturers, investors and infrastructure developers to government entities and smart technology providers. In doing so, it strengthens Dubai’s position as a global hub for electric and smart mobility and supports the development of an integrated ecosystem for partnerships, investment and innovation in sustainable transport.The event offers an opportunity to strengthen dialogue across the sector, explore investment and partnership opportunities, and address the challenges associated with the wider adoption of electric vehicles, including the development of charging infrastructure, battery management, vehicle-grid integration, and the advancement of technologies and systems supporting electric mobility.The exhibition and conference also underscore Dubai’s drive to build an integrated electric mobility ecosystem that extends beyond vehicles themselves to encompass infrastructure, technology, energy, smart systems, specialised talent and investment partnerships, further strengthening the emirate’s readiness for the next phase of transformation in the transport sector.Supported by Dubai’s strategic location, advanced infrastructure, extensive experience in operating clean-energy vehicles and broad network of international partnerships, the event will further strengthen the emirate’s position as a global hub for developing, testing and adopting electric and smart mobility solutions, while supporting efforts to build a more sustainable and efficient future for transport and mobility.RTA continues to strengthen the emirate’s position as a global capital for sustainable and environmentally friendly mobility through an integrated strategy aimed at achieving a full transition to zero-emission public transport by 2050.RTA is translating this future-focused vision into action through a comprehensive framework spanning vehicles, public buses and marine transport, in line with the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and UAE Net Zero 2050 Strategy.As part of its efforts to modernise the taxi and limousine sectors, RTA has increased the share of environmentally friendly hybrid vehicles in Dubai’s taxi and limousine fleet to more than 72 percent. Electric vehicles now account for 19 percent of the fleet, exceeding the target set for 2026. RTA has also developed an ambitious operational plan to convert the entire taxi and limousine fleet to electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles by 2040.In parallel, RTA is expanding the testing and deployment of autonomous electric vehicles in collaboration with leading global companies, while developing advanced fast-charging infrastructure across public parking areas and major transport facilities.In the public bus sector, RTA has made significant progress in replacing conventional buses with advanced electric models specifically designed to operate in the region’s climatic conditions. RTA continues to conduct operational trials of the latest fast-charging and opportunity-charging technologies, while equipping bus stations with renewable energy systems and high-capacity power supply equipment to ensure efficient and sustainable round-the-clock operations.RTA’s efforts also extend beyond land transport to the marine transport sector, which has undergone a major transformation through the development of traditional abras and modern marine transport modes operating across Dubai Creek and Dubai Water Canal using environmentally friendly electric and hydrogen-powered propulsion systems. These modes help reduce carbon emissions and noise pollution while preserving the heritage identity of Dubai’s iconic marine transport and providing passengers and tourists with a smooth, quiet travel experience that enhances quality of life.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai launches agentic AI accelerator to transform public-facing government services
source_snapshot.text: Dubai has launched a new accelerator programme to apply agentic artificial intelligence across government services, marking a significant step in the emirate's push to future-proof public sector operations. The Dubai Future Foundation announced the agentic AI for Government Services Accelerator under its Dubai Future Accelerators initiative. The programme will help government entities create prototypes to use in AI-powered services within significantly shorter time frames. In its first phase, the accelerator will bring together 33 Dubai government entities and assess more than 300 public-facing use cases to identify those with the greatest potential for agentic AI development. The project is being organised by the Dubai Centre for Artificial Intelligence in collaboration with Digital Dubai and the Dubai Electronic Security Centre. Participants will work alongside technology companies certified under the Dubai AI Seal, a recognition programme designed to identify trusted AI firms operating in the emirate. Agentic AI is an advanced form of autonomous artificial intelligence that can work independently without constant human supervision. Unlike traditional or standard generative AI, which responds to prompts and waits for the next instruction, agentic AI can act like an independent project manager, making decisions and executing them through external software systems. When given an objective, rather than trying to solve the entire problem immediately, agentic AI breaks the goal into smaller tasks, allowing it to process a number of ways to reach the end goal. It evaluates the various paths as it goes and corrects mistakes as and when needed. It is this ability to monitor its own progress that makes it particularly useful. If there is a problem, it does not wait for a human to fix it, but self-corrects in real time, allowing it to take on complex tasks that can last for hours or days. Hamad Al Mansoori, Director General of Digital Dubai, said the programme represented a shift from responding to residents' needs to anticipating them. “The future of digital government cannot be shaped by any single entity; it requires an integrated ecosystem that brings together expertise, data and capabilities around a common goal,” he said. Khalfan Belhoul, chief executive of Dubai Future Foundation, said the launch aligned with directives from Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed , Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Defence and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of DFF, to position Dubai as the world's leading city in the adoption of agentic AI across government services. “Artificial intelligence has opened new horizons for governments to imagine the future, design next-generation solutions and services, and bring them to life,” Mr Belhoul said. “Government entities can now significantly shorten traditional development cycles and processes, enabling them to enhance the quality and effectiveness of their services within much shorter time frames. “Dubai has all the foundations required to lead this transformation, including an agile regulatory ecosystem and advanced infrastructure that enable government entities to rapidly advance the quality of their services.” Yousuf Al Shaibani, chief executive of the Dubai Electronic Security Centre, emphasised that cybersecurity must be embedded throughout the process. “Artificial intelligence is reshaping how government services are designed and delivered. Cybersecurity cannot be an afterthought in the adoption of AI. It must be embedded at every stage, from planning and design to operation and monitoring,” Mr Al Shaibani said.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Supreme Council of Energy highlights best operational practices to enhance safety and compliance in petroleum products trading
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 5th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Dubai Supreme Council of Energy (DSCE) emphasised the significance of maintaining safety and compliance standards across petroleum products trading activities and fostering safe operating practices among companies and establishments within the sector. To ensure this, the Council seeks to maintain secure and efficient operations across every stage of petroleum products trading, including storage, transport, distribution and supply.This forms a part of DSCE’s regulatory and supervisory role, and its commitment to ensuring that petroleum products are traded in Dubai according to the highest standards of safety and compliance. It further aligns with the provisions of Executive Council Resolution No. 85 of 2025 on the Regulation of Petroleum Products Trading in Dubai, alongside all the resolutions, requirements and technical standards approved under it.Ahmed Butti Al Muhairbi, Secretary General of the Dubai Supreme Council of Energy and Chairman of the Dubai Regulatory Committee for Petroleum Products, highlighted that Executive Council Resolution No. 85 of 2025 provides an integrated regulatory framework to improve the efficiency and reliability of Dubai’s petroleum products trading sector. He noted that the resolution achieves this by regulating relevant sector activities, strengthening compliance with safety requirements and technical standards, and curbing unauthorised practices.Al Muhairbi added: “Compliance with regulatory, technical and safety standards remains a primary responsibility for all entities within the petroleum products trading sector. This requires companies to maintain the validity of all necessary licenses and permits, ensuring that facilities and transport methods strictly adhere to approved requirements. It also requires proper implementation of operations, maintenance and safety procedures aligned with defined requirements, along with maintenance of relevant records and documentation. Ultimately, this approach enhances operational safety, mitigates risks, and actively protects personnel, facilities, and the environment.”DSCE explained that implementing best operational practices begins with full compliance regarding licensing requirements, approved specifications and technical requirements. This includes utilising authorised facilities and transport methods that meet all safety metrics, alongside execution of inspection and maintenance activities in line with approved requirements. Furthermore, it entails providing appropriate personnel training, maintaining necessary records and documentation, and ensuring strict adherence to safe operating procedures throughout all stages of petroleum products trading.DSCE emphasised that key practices requiring close monitoring and attention within the petroleum products trading sector include the use of unauthorised facilities or transport methods, non-compliance with storage and transport regulations, trading in products that do not conform to approved specifications, and shortcomings in documenting product sources and movements.Inspection campaigns and operations carried out by DSCE, in collaboration with relevant government entities, have discovered cases involving the storage or trading of diesel at unlicensed facilities and its transport using methods that do not meet approved requirements. Such practices pose significant safety risks, including petroleum product leaks and their potential environmental impact, underlining the significance of full compliance with regulatory and operational requirements throughout all stages of petroleum products trading.DSCE has urged companies and establishments within the sector to strengthen compliance with approved regulatory and technical frameworks, ensure that licences and permits remain valid, verify that products conform to UAE-approved specifications, and utilise safe and authorised facilities for storage. The Council also underlined the importance of operating vehicles and using transport methods that meet approved requirements, implementing safe operating procedures during transport and handling, complying with maintenance and inspection programs, and significantly upgrading emergency response readiness across all infrastructure and transport assets.The Council continues to strengthen its field monitoring framework through the permanent joint field inspection team for the petroleum products trading sector, in coordination with relevant government entities. This collaborative effort supports integrated oversight initiatives and enhances the effective implementation of regulatory requirements. Furthermore, these inspections and monitoring operations ensure compliance with approved requirements, identify unauthorised practices, and facilitate the execution of necessary measures in accordance with applicable regulations and resolutions.Additionally, the Council conducts targeted inspections and monitoring campaigns, especially in the diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sectors, to verify compliance with approved specifications and enhance operational safety. Its comprehensive approach seamlessly combines regulation, monitoring, inspections, and coordination with relevant companies and authorities, thereby contributing to a safe, organised environment for petroleum products trading while protecting personnel, infrastructure and the environment.Since commencing operations in July 2022, the permanent joint field inspection team has conducted 449 joint inspection campaigns within the LPG sector. These operations form a core part of the efforts to restrict unauthorised practices and reinforce compliance with safety requirements and applicable regulations.Within the framework of Executive Council Resolution No. 85 of 2025 on the Regulation of Petroleum Products Trading in the Emirate of Dubai, this regulatory and monitoring approach reflects the DSCE’s unwavering commitment to establishing an integrated framework for sector regulation. Built upon the pillars of strong governance, transparency and effective oversight, this strategy actively contributes to stopping illegal trading, safeguarding personnel, property, and the environment, and enhancing the efficiency of the energy sector. Ultimately, these efforts reinforce Dubai’s position as a leading global city in applying regulatory and operational best practices while advancing sustainable development.

To ensure this, the Council seeks to maintain secure and efficient operations across every stage of petroleum products trading, including storage, transport, distribution and supply.This forms a part of DSCE’s regulatory and supervisory role, and its commitment to ensuring that petroleum products are traded in Dubai according to the highest standards of safety and compliance.
It further aligns with the provisions of Executive Council Resolution No.

85 of 2025 on the Regulation of Petroleum Products Trading in Dubai, alongside all the resolutions, requirements and technical standards approved under it.Ahmed Butti Al Muhairbi, Secretary General of the Dubai Supreme Council of Energy and Chairman of the Dubai Regulatory Committee for Petroleum Products, highlighted that Executive Council Resolution No.
85 of 2025 provides an integrated regulatory framework to improve the efficiency and reliability of Dubai’s petroleum products trading sector.

He noted that the resolution achieves this by regulating relevant sector activities, strengthening compliance with safety requirements and technical standards, and curbing unauthorised practices.Al Muhairbi added: “Compliance with regulatory, technical and safety standards remains a primary responsibility for all entities within the petroleum products trading sector.
This requires companies to maintain the validity of all necessary licenses and permits, ensuring that facilities and transport methods strictly adhere to approved requirements.
It also requires proper implementation of operations, maintenance and safety procedures aligned with defined requirements, along with maintenance of relevant records and documentation.

Ultimately, this approach enhances operational safety, mitigates risks, and actively protects personnel, facilities, and the environment.”DSCE explained that implementing best operational practices begins with full compliance regarding licensing requirements, approved specifications and technical requirements.
This includes utilising authorised facilities and transport methods that meet all safety metrics, alongside execution of inspection and maintenance activities in line with approved requirements.

Furthermore, it entails providing appropriate personnel training, maintaining necessary records and documentation, and ensuring strict adherence to safe operating procedures throughout all stages of petroleum products trading.DSCE emphasised that key practices requiring close monitoring and attention within the petroleum products trading sector include the use of unauthorised facilities or transport methods, non-compliance with storage and transport regulations, trading in products that do not conform to approved specifications, and shortcomings in documenting product sources and movements.Inspection campaigns and operations carried out by DSCE, in collaboration with relevant government entities, have discovered cases involving the storage or trading of diesel at unlicensed facilities and its transport using methods that do not meet approved requirements.

The Council also underlined the importance of operating vehicles and using transport methods that meet approved requirements, implementing safe operating procedures during transport and handling, complying with maintenance and inspection programs, and significantly upgrading emergency response readiness across all infrastructure and transport assets.The Council continues to strengthen its field monitoring framework through the permanent joint field inspection team for the petroleum products trading sector, in coordination with relevant government entities.
This collaborative effort supports integrated oversight initiatives and enhances the effective implementation of regulatory requirements.

Furthermore, these inspections and monitoring operations ensure compliance with approved requirements, identify unauthorised practices, and facilitate the execution of necessary measures in accordance with applicable regulations and resolutions.Additionally, the Council conducts targeted inspections and monitoring campaigns, especially in the diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sectors, to verify compliance with approved specifications and enhance operational safety.

source_snapshot.title: DIB, Expo City Dubai partner to advance off-plan home financing
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 6th October, 2026 (WAM) -- DIB, the world’s leading Islamic financial group and the largest Islamic bank in the UAE, has entered into a strategic partnership with Expo City Dubai to offer eligible buyers Home Financing for properties under construction within Expo City Dubai. The agreement supports DIB’s strategy to expand its Home Finance proposition through strategic partnerships with leading developers and government-related entities across the UAE.The partnership marks an important collaboration with one of Dubai’s most distinctive developments. Building on the legacy of Expo 2020 Dubai, the first World Expo held in the Middle East, Africa and South Asia, Expo City Dubai is evolving into a sustainable, master-planned urban community encompassing residential, commercial and cultural developments, playing a key role in Dubai’s future growth.Once a DIB-approved project has reached at least 35% construction completion and the customer has paid at least 50% of the purchase price, DIB can finance up to 50% of the property value. Full monthly instalments begin at handover or within 24 months of taking the finance, whichever comes first. Financing is available for up to 25 years, subject to DIB's eligibility, credit, regulatory and final approval requirements. The proposition is open to eligible UAE nationals, residents and non-residents and does not require a salary transfer.Commenting on the partnership, Sanjay Malhotra - Chief Consumer Banking Officer at DIB, said, “Expo City Dubai represents one of the most distinctive chapters in Dubai’s urban story, and we are proud to bring DIB’s Home Finance expertise to a destination built on such a strong legacy. Through this partnership, DIB customers will benefit from tailored financing solutions designed to make homeownership at one of Dubai’s most strategically located destinations more accessible, particularly as demand for off-plan properties continues to grow. Eligible Expo City Dubai buyers can arrange finance during construction, pay only the profit amount during that period and move to full instalments at handover or within 24 months. The value of the proposition is simple: earlier clarity on one of the biggest financial commitments a customer will make.”Ahmed Al Khatib, Chief Development and Delivery Officer at Expo City Dubai, said, “Partnering with a premier institution such as DIB significantly enhances Expo City Dubai’s ability to offer buyers a smooth, simple and hassle-free journey to home ownership. DIB’s Shariah-compliant home financing solutions will empower more investors to join our community in a collaboration that reflects trust in Expo City’s long-term vision and confidence in Dubai’s real estate landscape.”

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Culture, World Cities Culture Forum announce Global Fellowship cohort comprising next generation of cultural policymakers
source_snapshot.text: Dubai, 6th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture) and the World Cities Culture Forum have announced the cohort of the Global Fellowship, an international leadership programme designed to develop the next generation of cultural policymakers and civic leaders for culture. Bringing together 20 mid-career professionals, the programme will strengthen their ability to shape cultural policy and deliver projects that respond to their cities’ priorities. It supports Dubai’s ambition to serve as a global cultural reference, a leader in innovation and a driver of the creative economy grounded in Emirati heritage.Co-founded by Dubai Culture and the World Cities Culture Forum, the first-of-its-kind programme is a legacy of the 13th World Cities Culture Summit, held in Dubai in 2024 under the theme ‘Tomorrow’s Culture: How Will the Next Generation Shape Our World?’ The summit marked the event’s first edition in the Middle East and North Africa. The Fellowship’s academic programme, in collaboration with the University of Oxford’s Gardens, Libraries and Museums and the Aspen Institute, brings together international expertise in leadership development, cultural policy and city development.The cohort includes five fellows from Dubai Government entities: Hesham Al Olama, CEO of the Media Development Sector at the Dubai Media Council; Afnan Abdulla, Director of the Asset Management and Logistics Department at Dubai Culture; Mozah Lootah, Senior Project Manager in the Visual Arts Department at Dubai Culture; Noora Bin Kalban, Director of Exploration Policies and Programs at Dubai Knowledge and Human Development Authority; and Hessa Aljarwan, Manager of Studies and Policies, Quality of Life, at the Roads and Transport Authority in Dubai. The remaining 15 fellows were selected through a competitive process from the World Cities Culture Forum network, with each representing a different member city.Over six months, fellows will combine international learning, mentorship and peer exchange with the development of a project for their city. Following onboarding, they will participate in dedicated sessions at the 15th World Cities Culture Summit in Tokyo from 28 to 30 October, joining more than 150 cultural leaders from around the world.The fellowship will feature online masterclasses and an immersive residency, drawing on the expertise of leading figures in cultural policy and city leadership. Contributors include Justine Simons OBE, Founder and Chair of the World Cities Culture Forum and London’s Deputy Mayor for Culture and the Creative Industries; Anne Hidalgo, former Mayor of Paris; Yvonne Aki-Sawyerr, Mayor of Freetown; Gail Lord, global cultural consultant and museum planner; and Ricky Burdett, Director of LSE Cities and Professor of Urban Studies.Hala Badri, Director-General of Dubai Culture, highlighted the role of international cooperation in strengthening cultural leadership and connecting local priorities with global expertise. She said, “Investing in people is central to Dubai’s cultural ambitions and to our contribution to the future of culture in cities. Through the Global Fellowship, we are giving emerging leaders the opportunity to learn from one another, develop their ideas and translate that knowledge into policies and projects that serve their communities. We want fellows to leave with the confidence, relationships and practical skills to strengthen the role of culture in sustainable urban development and quality of life.”She added, “The fellowship also creates opportunities for talent from Dubai to benefit from international experience and share the emirate’s own approaches to cultural development. Each fellow brings a distinct understanding of their city, and that exchange of perspectives can lead to better-informed decisions and new ways of working. By connecting these professionals with experienced leaders and institutions, we aim to build lasting relationships that support their work and the communities they serve.”Justine Simons OBE, Founder, World Cities Culture Forum, and Deputy Mayor for Culture and the Creative Industries, London, said, “All around the world, city leaders are championing culture and using the power they have, to make real change. Their leadership environment is unique – it’s a place where civic responsibility, policy, politics and cultural transformation come together. We know culture can play an even greater role in the success of cities around the world, growing economies, bringing communities together, improving our health and quality of life – but only if we have great leaders in the right places, able to unlock its full potential. So, I am hugely proud of this new Global Fellowship, the first of its kind, as it responds to the growing need to nurture the next generation of civic leaders for culture.”He added, “Co-founded with Dubai Culture and Arts Authority as a legacy of the 2024 World Cities Culture Summit, this bespoke programme connects emerging leaders with our global network of experts and will build the talent, skills and resilience needed to achieve impact at a city level. Congratulations to our founding cohort of twenty exceptional cultural leaders from across our global network."From November 2026 to March 2027, fellows will take part in online masterclasses examining the practical demands of cultural leadership. Topics will include the political forces shaping cultural policy and the role of public-private partnerships; integrating culture into urban planning and infrastructure; understanding power, influence and authority across arts and government; strengthening cross-departmental collaboration; and sustaining effective cultural leadership over the long term.Each fellow will develop a strategic cultural project that addresses an opportunity or challenge in their city, supported by peer exchange, expert guidance and one-to-one mentorship from experienced leaders in the World Cities Culture Forum network. Defined at the outset, these projects will develop through the Tokyo summit and online masterclasses, advance during the Dubai residency, and move towards implementation at the programme’s conclusion. This process will help fellows refine their leadership approach and apply their learning within their professional and civic contexts.The programme will conclude with a five-day residency in Dubai in spring 2027. Fellows will work on their projects, engage with cultural institutions and explore the emirate’s approaches to cultural development, innovation and collaboration across sectors. The residency supports Dubai Culture’s commitment to talent development, knowledge exchange and intercultural dialogue, in line with its 2026–2033 Strategy and three pillars: Global Cultural Leadership; a Robust Creative Ecosystem; and Cultural Identity, Diversity and Inclusivity.Developed in response to the growing responsibilities of cultural policymakers, the fellowship recognises culture’s contribution to economic development, social cohesion, and quality of life. It will help participants build international professional relationships and draw on practices from different cities to develop solutions for their communities.The inaugural cohort includes representatives of Austin, Boston, Bratislava, Busan, Edinburgh, Guangzhou, Johannesburg, Kyiv, London, Milan, Rio de Janeiro, Seoul, Toronto, Vienna and Warsaw apart from Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: Urban Planning Committee, RTA and Dubai Municipality launch new addressing identity
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 7th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Supreme Committee for Urban Planning, in coordination with Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) and Dubai Municipality, has launched a new visual identity and enhanced addressing system for areas across the Emirate of Dubai. The initiative includes the installation and replacement of area identification signs, internal street name signs, and house number plates, featuring unified designs and colours that reflect the geographic characteristics of each area.Developed through a specialist consultant in wayfinding and addressing design, the new system will help facilitate the identification of locations and improve accessibility, while enhancing the visual appeal of streets, residential neighbourhoods, and commercial districts.The launch forms part of efforts to establish an integrated and clear addressing system that keeps pace with Dubai’s rapid urban development. Going beyond its traditional wayfinding role, the new system is designed to become an integral component of the visual identity of Dubai’s areas, while contributing to the enhancement of streets and road facilities and highlighting the geographic and urban characteristics that distinguish communities across the emirate.The implementation plan covers 186 areas distributed across 19 sectors throughout Dubai, under a phased programme that will begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 and continue through 2030. The first phase of the project will commence this year and will include the installation and replacement of more than 2,000 signs across five areas: Za’abeel 1, Za’abeel 2, Nad Al Sheba, Al Khawaneej 1, and Nazwa, in accordance with the approved visual identity for each area.The new visual identity incorporates five colours specifically designed to reflect the character and geographic features of Dubai’s various areas, providing each with a distinctive visual signature while maintaining a clear and consistent addressing system across the emirate. The selected colours have been carefully aligned with the nature of each area. For example, blue represents areas located close to the sea, while gold symbolises areas characterised by a desert environment, reflecting the diversity of Dubai’s landscapes and urban fabric.The new identity encompasses sector and area identification signs, internal street name signs, and house number plates, with designs and colour schemes developed to achieve visual integration across all components of the addressing system. Future project deliverables will extend the identity to bus stops, smart applications, and area map boards. In addition, QR codes will be introduced to provide information about sectors and areas, the meanings behind street and area names, points of interest, and other relevant location-related content.In coordination with Dubai Municipality, RTA has established a set of criteria to determine implementation priorities across the emirate. These include urban growth and population density, the vibrancy and centrality of areas, the presence of residential and tourist attractions, and the proportion of streets that have not yet been formally addressed. This approach ensures that project implementation aligns with urban development trends and the needs of residents across Dubai.As part of the continued rollout of the new addressing identity, RTA has coordinated with Dubai Municipality to complete and approve the final designs for house number plates. These plates will feature each property's Makani number and corresponding QR Code, with colours harmonised with those of the new addressing signs to enhance visual integration, reinforce a unified identity, and further facilitate location identification.

evidence_passages.text: Urban Planning Committee, RTA and Dubai Municipality launch new addressing identity

DUBAI, 7th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Supreme Committee for Urban Planning, in coordination with Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) and Dubai Municipality, has launched a new visual identity and enhanced addressing system for areas across the Emirate of Dubai.

The initiative includes the installation and replacement of area identification signs, internal street name signs, and house number plates, featuring unified designs and colours that reflect the geographic characteristics of each area.Developed through a specialist consultant in wayfinding and addressing design, the new system will help facilitate the identification of locations and improve accessibility, while enhancing the visual appeal of streets, residential neighbourhoods, and commercial districts.The launch forms part of efforts to establish an integrated and clear addressing system that keeps pace with Dubai’s rapid urban development.

Going beyond its traditional wayfinding role, the new system is designed to become an integral component of the visual identity of Dubai’s areas, while contributing to the enhancement of streets and road facilities and highlighting the geographic and urban characteristics that distinguish communities across the emirate.The implementation plan covers 186 areas distributed across 19 sectors throughout Dubai, under a phased programme that will begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 and continue through 2030.

The first phase of the project will commence this year and will include the installation and replacement of more than 2,000 signs across five areas: Za’abeel 1, Za’abeel 2, Nad Al Sheba, Al Khawaneej 1, and Nazwa, in accordance with the approved visual identity for each area.The new visual identity incorporates five colours specifically designed to reflect the character and geographic features of Dubai’s various areas, providing each with a distinctive visual signature while maintaining a clear and consistent addressing system across the emirate.
The selected colours have been carefully aligned with the nature of each area.

For example, blue represents areas located close to the sea, while gold symbolises areas characterised by a desert environment, reflecting the diversity of Dubai’s landscapes and urban fabric.The new identity encompasses sector and area identification signs, internal street name signs, and house number plates, with designs and colour schemes developed to achieve visual integration across all components of the addressing system.
Future project deliverables will extend the identity to bus stops, smart applications, and area map boards.

In addition, QR codes will be introduced to provide information about sectors and areas, the meanings behind street and area names, points of interest, and other relevant location-related content.In coordination with Dubai Municipality, RTA has established a set of criteria to determine implementation priorities across the emirate.

These include urban growth and population density, the vibrancy and centrality of areas, the presence of residential and tourist attractions, and the proportion of streets that have not yet been formally addressed.

This approach ensures that project implementation aligns with urban development trends and the needs of residents across Dubai.As part of the continued rollout of the new addressing identity, RTA has coordinated with Dubai Municipality to complete and approve the final designs for house number plates.

These plates will feature each property's Makani number and corresponding QR Code, with colours harmonised with those of the new addressing signs to enhance visual integration, reinforce a unified identity, and further facilitate location identification.

source_snapshot.title: Theyab bin Tahnoon inaugurates 15th season of Dubai Miracle Garden
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Sheikh Theyab bin Tahnoon bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, Chairman of Miracle Group, today inaugurated the 15th season of Dubai Miracle Garden, the world’s largest natural flower garden, under the theme ‘Fifteen Years, Blooming Together’.Running until 31st May 2027, the new season features more than 200 million flowers across 72,000 square metres and, for the first time, will introduce a new theme each week throughout the season.The inauguration was attended by Hamdan Al Kaabi, Vice Chairman of Miracle Group; Eng. Mohammed Zaher Hammadih, Group CEO of Miracle Group; senior executives of the Group; and representatives from Dubai’s tourism and hospitality sectors.Sheikh Theyab bin Tahnoon bin Mohammed Al Nahyan highlighted the ongoing efforts to enhance Dubai Miracle Garden’s appeal as one of Dubai’s leading attractions, distinguished by its unique floral displays and creative designs.He said, “Over its fifteen seasons, Dubai Miracle Garden has grown alongside Dubai, becoming part of the memories of its residents and visitors. This season is dedicated to the community that has contributed to its success, particularly the families and residents who continue to return year after year.”The weekly themes will reflect the national and cultural calendar, bringing the UAE’s diverse communities together through flowers, art and music.The opening months of the season will focus on wellness, culture and community, with activities marking Pink October, United Nations Day, UAE Flag Day and Diwali. The programme will also feature live music, family activities and fitness events as part of the Dubai Fitness Challenge. Dedicated events will also mark Commemoration Day and Eid Al Etihad.Eng. Mohammed Zaher Hammadih said, “As we mark our 15th season, Dubai Miracle Garden continues to bring people together through shared experiences. Our weekly programme gives families a new reason to return, with cultural celebrations, live entertainment and activities to enjoy throughout the season.”The garden showcases more than 150 flower varieties alongside its signature floral structures, which have earned it multiple Guinness World Records.Since opening in 2013, Dubai Miracle Garden has welcomed millions of visitors and established itself as one of the region’s leading family attractions, contributing to Dubai’s appeal as a global tourism destination.Dubai Miracle Garden will welcome visitors daily from 8 October 2026 to 31st May 2027. Opening hours are from 9am to 9pm on weekdays and from 9am to 11pm on weekends. Entry is free for children under the age of three.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality launches ‘A Generation for a Greater Tomorrow’ initiative
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality has launched the community initiative ‘A Generation for a Greater Tomorrow’, bringing children and their families together through an interactive experience that introduces them to the Municipality’s diverse areas of work and demonstrates how municipal services contribute to the way the city functions and supports everyday life. The initiative will take place at City Centre Mirdif from 7 to 11 October, from 10:00am to 10:00pm.The initiative combines education, exploration and recreation through a series of interactive stations designed to help children gain knowledge and develop skills through age-appropriate activities, games and practical experiences. The programme also provides opportunities for families to participate together, in line with the UAE’s Year of the Family and its emphasis on strengthening family participation and engagement.Through a range of experiences, children can explore different aspects of municipal work and gain a better understanding of their connection to everyday life. An agriculture-focused station introduces children to local plant species and the basics of growing seedlings, preparing soil, and applying effective irrigation and cultivation methods, highlighting the role of agriculture and green spaces in the city.The initiative also introduces children to basic health and safety practices at home and in public spaces. Activities cover common household tools and key safety principles relating to roads, beaches, parks and other public places, helping children connect what they learn with situations they may encounter in their daily lives.A dedicated platform focuses on communication, creativity and content creation, giving children an opportunity to develop their speaking and presentation skills, express their ideas and explore different ways of creating and sharing content.The programme also features interactive digital games that introduce children to municipal services in an accessible and age-appropriate way. One game explores health and safety management, including public health services related to veterinary care and pet welfare, while another introduces waste management and the importance of proper waste handling in maintaining the city’s cleanliness and sustainability.An interactive laboratory platform gives children an introduction to the world of laboratories through simple scientific experiments, while demonstrating the role of laboratories in municipal work and their relevance to everyday life.Through ‘A Generation for a Greater Tomorrow’, Dubai Municipality aims to strengthen children’s understanding of municipal work while giving them opportunities to explore their interests and develop skills across different fields and areas of specialisation. The initiative also provides an opportunity to engage with the aspirations of the next generation and strengthen their connection with the work that contributes to developing Dubai and enhancing the quality of life of its residents, supporting the continued development of a more attractive, sustainable and liveable city.

source_snapshot.title: Maktoum bin Mohammed reviews Dubai economic, financial indicators
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, First Deputy Ruler of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Finance and Chairman of the Higher Committee for the Development of the Economic and Financial Sector, chaired a meeting of the Committee to review the latest performance indicators across Dubai’s economic and financial sectors.The meeting highlighted the emirate’s progress across several global financial competitiveness indices and reviewed proposed strategic directions to reinforce Dubai’s standing as a leading, integrated global hub for gold.H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum emphasised that Dubai, guided by the vision and directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, continues to advance its economic competitiveness, develop its financial and economic sectors, build integrated ecosystems to drive sustainable growth, and further reinforce its position among the world’s leading hubs for business, finance and trade.H.H. stated: “Guided by the vision and directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, we continue Dubai’s journey of economic diversification, competitiveness and sustainability. We continue to reinforce the emirate’s standing as a global hub for business, finance and trade by developing more competitive economic and financial sectors that are better capable of attracting investments, talent and global companies.”During the meeting, the Committee reviewed Dubai’s competitiveness indicators in the financial sector, which showed the emirate ranking first globally in FinTech on the Global Financial Centres Index (GFCI) published in September 2026, rising from fifth place in March 2026.Dubai also advanced to become second globally in Professional Services (up from fourth) and sixth in reputation (up from eighth), reflecting its continuous rise among top international financial centres.For the fourth consecutive time, Dubai maintained its leading position among global financial centres expected to become more significant over the next two to three years, in a testament to global confidence in its ability to sustain growth and strengthen its role in the global financial economy.In the virtual assets sector, the number of licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) under the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) rose to 52, with assets under management reaching AED28 billion. Furthermore, trading volumes among licensed VASPs reached approximately AED7.43 trillion over the past 12 months, highlighting the sector's rapid growth and Dubai's evolving regulatory ecosystem.Financial market indicators highlighted sustained momentum across the Dubai Financial Market (DFM), with market capitalisation reaching AED993.1 billion by the end of the third quarter of 2026. DFM also saw a 24.5% surge in average daily trading values, while institutional trading accounted for 71% of total trading value.DFM attracted 55,462 new investors during the first nine months of 2026, with international investors representing 72.1% of new entrants to the market, reflecting a broadening investor base and the market's strong appeal to global capital.Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) continues to reinforce its role as a premier platform for businesses and financial services, hosting over 10,000 active registered companies. These include 592 wealth and asset management firms, alongside 1,933 FinTech and innovation firms, and the largest concentration of hedge funds in the region, underscoring the ongoing expansion of Dubai's financial ecosystem and the growing base of international institutions leveraging the emirate as a launchpad for their regional and global operations.Reinforcing Dubai’s position as a global hub for goldAmong the strategic priorities addressed during the meeting, the Committee reviewed statistics on the gold sector in Dubai and the UAE, as well as proposed directions to develop a comprehensive strategy that reinforces Dubai’s position as a leading global hub for gold. The proposed strategy spans all components of the value chain, from supply, refining and trading, to storage, financing, pricing, digital tokenisation and retail.Figures reviewed by the Committee showed that Dubai’s foreign gold trade reached approximately AED1 trillion in 2025, an increase of 60% year-on-year. The volume of physical gold traded in the UAE reached around 2,750 tonnes, placing the country second globally among physical gold trading hubs, with an estimated 13–15% of globally traded gold passing through Dubai annually.Dubai’s geographic location reinforces its role as a vital link connecting bullion supply sources in Africa and Central Asia with major demand markets in India, China and across the globe. The precious metals, gemstones and diamonds ecosystem at the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC) comprises over 1,500 member companies, while the Dubai Gold District, launched in 2026, hosts more than 1,000 retail gold and jewellery traders.This ecosystem has witnessed the launch of the UAE Good Delivery Standard and the establishment of the UAE Bullion Market Committee in 2021, followed by the launch of the Dubai Gold District in 2026, marking continuous institutional and regulatory development.Six key directions under the Dubai Gold StrategyThe Committee reviewed six proposed strategic directions for the development of the Dubai Gold Strategy. The first focuses on developing an integrated global market for gold trading by expanding market depth and connecting producers, refineries and buyers across Africa, the Middle East and Asia.The second direction focuses on strengthening Dubai’s position as a global hub for gold financing by exploring opportunities in gold-related financing, clearing, collateralisation, hedging and institutional trading.The third aims to solidify Dubai’s status as a trusted and neutral centre for gold storage, by enhancing secure storage capabilities for institutional and sovereign assets. The fourth direction addresses boosting the competitiveness of gold traded through Dubai by advancing traceability, transparency standards and advanced practices.The fifth direction addresses supporting Dubai’s role in gold price discovery by examining financial instruments and platforms that leverage market depth and liquidity. The sixth direction focuses on reinforcing Dubai’s standing as a premier global destination for jewellery and end-user demand, driving retail trade and consumer demand while enhancing market appeal for traders and investors.The meeting also approved the establishment of a committee chaired by His Excellency Abdulla bin Damithan to drive the execution of the approved strategic direction for the Dubai Gold Strategy, further develop and refine its initiatives, and coordinate with relevant entities to establish a clear implementation roadmap.The committee’s responsibilities include identifying actionable initiatives and defining roles and partners, as well as proposing a governance model and execution timelines. This approach ensures a structured transition from strategic directions to informed, adoption-ready initiatives, while fostering public-private sector partnerships.

source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Health Authority (DHA) has welcomed 49 students to the 11th cohort of the Tibb wa Uloom (Medicine and Sciences), its study sponsorship programme for Emirati students.The programme targets high-achieving secondary school graduates and university students who wish to study health specialities.The students met Dr Alawi AlSheikh-Ali, Director-General of DHA, at a gathering during which the sponsorship contracts for the new cohort were signed.Since the programme launched in 2016, a total of 618 students have enrolled to date, including 297 graduates. This reflects DHA's continued efforts to support and develop Emirati talent in health specialities and to prepare them to contribute to the progress of Dubai's health sector.Women made up 84.8 per cent of all students enrolled in the programme, compared with 15.2 per cent men.Medicine accounted for about 60 per cent of enrolments, followed by nursing and then allied health specialities, which include radiology, pharmacy, physiotherapy, nutrition and other health fields. The specialities covered by the programme have evolved over the years in line with health priorities and the needs of the sector. New specialities, including public health, have been added on the basis of a clinical capacity study, to ensure that Emirati talent is prepared in priority health areas.Asma Al Sharif, CEO of the Health Regulatory Sector at DHA, said that investing in Emirati talent is a cornerstone of the sustainable development of the health sector. She noted that enabling Emirati students to build academic and professional pathways in health specialities helps supply the sector with qualified professionals who can meet its needs and future aspirations.She added, “The Tibb wa Uloom Programme is a long-term investment in Emirati talent. It begins by supporting students throughout their academic journey and extends to preparing them to contribute effectively to the health sector.”She noted that the arrival of the 11th cohort reflects the continuity of this investment and the programme's role in building a new generation of Emirati health professionals.Dr Khawla Al Hajaj, Director of the Medical Education and Research Department at DHA, said that the programme provides an integrated support system for Emirati students throughout their studies, combining academic sponsorship with training opportunities and practical development. This helps build their knowledge and skills and prepares them for the transition to professional life after they complete their studies.She added that the programme aims to attract and prepare Emirati students who wish to study health specialities, according to defined criteria, supporting the preparation of qualified Emirati professionals who can contribute effectively to the health sector.

source_snapshot.title: ISEA2026 Dubai connects global dialogue with artistic experiences across city
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 9th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture) has unveiled highlights of the artistic and academic programmes for the 31st International Symposium on Electronic/Emerging Art (ISEA2026 Dubai), taking place from 6 to 15 November 2026 under the theme ‘ELYAH: Constellating Place, Data and Identity’. Exploring the intersection of art, science and technology, the symposium supports Dubai Culture’s Digital Arts Roadmap by expanding opportunities for creative talent, encouraging experimentation and advancing the digital and emerging arts sector. It also reinforces Dubai’s position as a global cultural reference, a leader in innovation and a driver of the creative economy, rooted in Emirati heritage.ISEA2026 Dubai will adopt a hybrid format, combining an in-person artistic programme across multiple venues in Dubai with an online academic programme. This approach will enable artists, researchers and practitioners worldwide to exchange ideas and expertise while connecting international dialogue with artistic experiences across the city. The artistic programme attracted more than 1,000 submissions, with over 100 artworks shortlisted, while more than 150 submissions were shortlisted for the academic programme. The agenda includes over 140 academic papers, more than 40 artist talks and sessions, over 15 workshops, more than 10 panel discussions, seven Eco Labs and four special-track exhibitions and sessions.The academic programme will feature keynote addresses, paper presentations, specialist panels and artist talks. A key strand, the New Media Art Summit, will explore how artistic practices are evolving through digital networks, immersive environments, interactive media and artificial intelligence, connecting research and curatorial perspectives with artistic production, and Eco Labs will examine the relationship between ecological systems, technology and artistic practice.Across Dubai, the artistic programme will bring audiences into contact with digital and emerging art through exhibitions, performances and immersive experiences. The programme includes exhibitions across 20 locations including Al Safa Art & Design Library, Etihad Museum, Kanvas and Foundry Gallery, experiences at ARTE Museum, performances at TODA, and projection mapping at Al Wasl Dome. It will also feature the special track Evolving Calligraphy, Letter Art, Typography, including Calligraphy to Code, exploring how letterforms, writing systems and calligraphic traditions are being reimagined through digital and computational media. These activities will give residents and visitors opportunities to engage with contemporary artistic practice and explore how technology is shaping new forms of expression.Maitha Ali Al Blooshi, Director of the Emerging Arts Department at Dubai Culture, highlighted the symposium’s role in strengthening Dubai’s international cultural presence and connecting creative practices and disciplines. She said: “The response to ISEA2026 Dubai from around the world reflects the emirate’s ability to bring together artists, researchers and practitioners within an environment that encourages innovation and the exchange of ideas. The symposium will give local talent opportunities to learn, experiment and build connections with specialised international networks.”She added: “ISEA2026 Dubai brings together diverse disciplines and expertise, creating opportunities for art, research and technology to inform one another. Through collaboration and the development of artistic practice, it supports the growth and sustainability of the digital and emerging arts sector. It also provides a platform to explore how technology, imagination, knowledge and culture can come together to generate new ideas, artworks and creative approaches.”The theme ‘ELYAH: Constellating Place, Data and Identity’ connects four core academic tracks. Celestial Dialogues explores art, technology and the cosmic imagination, examining how the sky and planetary systems shape human experience and cultural meaning. Charting Constellations focuses on mapping, networks, place and identity, exploring the connections between people, data, geographies and stories. Eco-Tech Futures examines ecology, climate, and technological responsibility through artistic practice, while Starlinked Worlds explores how artificial intelligence, digital networks, and virtual environments are changing the ways people create, connect, and share cultural experiences.

source_snapshot.title: MBRSC, UNOOSA announce call for proposals for third opportunity under Payload Hosting Initiative
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 9th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre (MBRSC) and United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA) have announced the opening of applications for PHI-3, the third opportunity under the Payload Hosting Initiative (PHI), during the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) in Antalya, Türkiye.PHI is a joint programme by MBRSC in partnership with UNOOSA initiative ‘Access to Space for All’, which helps countries build practical space capabilities through hands-on opportunities. Through PHI, MBRSC develops and provides a 12U CubeSat platform to host innovative payloads and emerging space technologies from around the world. The programme offers partners the opportunity to test and validate their technologies in orbit, while participating in a real space mission supported by MBRSC’s technical and operational capabilities.Amer AlSayegh AlGhaferi, Assistant Director General of the Aerospace Engineering Sector, MBRSC, said, “PHI reflects our shared vision with UNOOSA to expand access to space and create meaningful opportunities for emerging space entities and nations to participate directly in real missions. Programmes such as PHI play an important role in broadening participation in the global space sector. By combining MBRSC’s satellite development and operational capabilities with UNOOSA’s international capacity-building framework, we are creating a pathway for new ideas, technologies and talent to reach space and generate knowledge that can support future missions and applications.”Aarti Holla-Maini, Director of UNOOSA, said, “Access to space is about much more than reaching orbit. It is about building the skills, experience and confidence that enable countries and institutions to develop their own space capabilities. PHI gives teams a practical first step on that journey. I strongly encourage teams from countries that have not yet had the opportunity to access space to apply for PHI-3.”The third mission builds on the first two PHI opportunities and continues the programme’s focus on providing an inclusive platform for testing, collaboration and innovation, enabling companies, universities, research centres and emerging space entities to contribute to the global space ecosystem. The programme also supports knowledge exchange across satellite design, manufacturing, testing, launch, operations and data analysis. The first satellite under the initiative, PHI-1 was launched in November 2025 with payloads from Bahrain Space Agency, Antarikchya Pratisthan Nepal, Sharjah Space and Astronomy Hub and the Centre. For PHI-2, the Technical University of Moldova (TUM) and Madari Space Limited of the UAE were selected to launch their payloads into space. Applications for PHI-3 will remain open until 6 April 2027. Following the submission period, proposals will be evaluated jointly by MBRSC and UNOOSA, with the selected awardees expected to be announced in the last quarter of 2027.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Cashless Strategy surpasses 2026 targets ahead of schedule
source_snapshot.text: Dubai Finance announced that the Dubai Cashless Strategy, launched by His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, in October 2024, has successfully exceeded its key targets ahead of its scheduled two-year timeframe. The results showed that Dubai’s cashless transactions index reached 90.1%, exceeding the 90% target set for 2026. The Digital Enablement Index for the government sector reached 100%, reflecting the availability of digital payment methods across institutions and businesses. Meanwhile, the community happiness index reached 90.1%, compared with the 90% target. The strategy’s final report, presented by Dubai Finance (DOF) to the Dubai Strategic Affairs Council, highlighted that the achievement reflects the emirate’s rapid progress towards establishing an integrated digital payments ecosystem and advancing digital enablement across both the government and private sectors. This progress has been driven by extensive partnerships among government entities, financial institutions, payment solution providers, and technology and financial services companies. The report showed that cashless payment initiatives contributed more than AED8 billion to the emirate’s economy. The strategic roadmap achieved strong results across the strategy’s three pillars, with 97% achieved in governance, 95% in society, and 93% in innovation, while operational business continuity was also maintained to ensure the sustainability of these results and maximise their long-term impact. Ambitious strategies His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum commended the combined efforts of the government and private sectors that contributed to this achievement. His Highness affirmed that the Strategy reflects the success of Dubai’s model, which is built on a clear vision, integrated roles between the government and private sectors, and the expanding use of technology and innovation to serve people and enhance economic competitiveness. "The Strategy reflects the success of Dubai’s model, which is built on a clear vision, integrated roles between the government and private sectors, and the expanding use of technology and innovation to serve people and enhance economic competitiveness" A global destination His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Dubai Free Zones Council, and Chairman and Chief Executive of Emirates Airlines and Emirates Group, said that the progress achieved by the Dubai Cashless Strategy enhances Dubai’s competitiveness as a global destination for business, investment, and tourism by providing a more seamless and efficient payment experience for the business community and visitors. His Highness underscored the importance of coordinating efforts across free zones, the aviation sector and other economic sectors to broaden the adoption of digital payment solutions, pointing out that this will facilitate the journeys of investors, customers, and visitors and support a more flexible and connected business environment. His Highness added that the partnership between the government and private sector is a key pillar in developing innovative solutions that meet the needs of global markets and reinforce Dubai’s position as an international hub for business, tourism, and the digital economy. The progress achieved by the Strategy enhances Dubai’s competitiveness as a global destination for business, investment, and tourism The government sector recorded advanced performance across cashless transformation indicators under the Dubai Cashless Strategy. Government cashless collections reached 99.66% during the first half of 2026, while the Digital Enablement Index of the government sector reached 100%. source_snapshot.title: Rental Disputes Centre settles 2,350 cases worth AED401 million in nine months
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 9th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Rental Disputes Centre (RDC) in Dubai concluded 2,350 rental disputes through amicable settlements worth a total of AED401 million in the first nine months of 2026, with an average resolution time of six days per case.The results highlight the effectiveness of the RDC's conciliation procedures in resolving rental disputes efficiently while protecting the legal rights of all parties.The figures also reflect the centre's efforts to improve dispute resolution mechanisms and judicial services amid continued growth in Dubai's rental market.Judge Abdulqader Mousa Mohammed, Chairman of the Rental Disputes Centre, said the results demonstrated the effectiveness of amicable settlements in resolving disputes swiftly while maintaining procedural standards and protecting the rights of those involved.He added that the RDC continues to develop its legal framework to support stable contractual relationships and strengthen confidence in Dubai's judicial system.Conciliation is a key alternative dispute resolution mechanism used by the RDC, allowing landlords and tenants to reach mutually agreed settlements without resorting to formal litigation.Settlement agreements are approved by a supervising judge, giving them the force of an enforceable legal instrument.The process also helps reduce the social and economic costs of prolonged disputes while promoting cooperation between the parties.The RDC said it remains committed to improving procedural efficiency, ensuring fair access to justice and promoting amicable settlements as an effective means of resolving rental disputes in Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: WETEX 2026 to spotlight AI, workplace health, safety
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) will organise the 28th edition of the Water, Energy, Technology and Environment Exhibition (WETEX) from 20th to 22nd October 2026 at the Dubai World Trade Centre, under the patronage of H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Dubai Supreme Council of Energy. The Health and Safety Hub at WETEX 2026 will host a range of activities and exhibitions, including the Health and Safety Conference, which will feature discussions on the latest developments in occupational health and safety in schools, homes and workplaces. The conference will bring together senior executives and experts from around the world in health, safety, wellbeing, emergency preparedness and emerging workplace risks. Discussions will focus on promoting health and wellbeing, using artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to manage risks, and improving quality of life through effective governance.Saeed Mohammed Al Tayer, MD and CEO of DEWA and Founder and Chairman of WETEX, said the exhibition supports the Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the National Strategy for Wellbeing 2031, which aims to position the UAE as a global leader in quality of life.He said the conference will highlight innovations and technologies that strengthen health and safety practices, protect people and safeguard property and the environment.The Health and Safety Conference’s panel discussions include ‘Discover the Future of HSE: Build Your Own AI + Vibe Coding Solution for Breakthrough Health & Safety Performance’, ‘Building Trust in AI Systems: Transparency, Ethics and Compliance and What They Mean in Practice’, ‘AI Fusion: Trust, Behaviour and Psychological Safety in the AI-Augmented Workplace’, ‘From Data to Prevention: Using AI and Analytics to Support Health, Safety and Environmental Decision Making’, ‘Workforce Wellbeing and Behavioural Safety in a Digital Era’, ‘AI and Robotics as Safety Enablers: Lessons from the Industrial Frontline’ and ‘Data-Driven Leadership: Turning Safety Data into Actionable Insights’.
