source_snapshot.title: The Ripe Market opens in Dubai: Here’s what to eat, shop, and do this season
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The aroma of freshly brewed coffee and baked cookies, the buzz of shoppers browsing independent brands, and the sound of children’s giggles and live entertainment set the scene as The Ripe Market returned to Dubai Police Academy Park in Umm Suqeim today, marking 15 years of bringing local businesses and communities together.The opening of the new season on October 10 has welcomed visitors back to one of Dubai’s familiar weekend destinations, where shopping, food, and family activities come together in an outdoor setting. With stalls to explore, food to enjoy, and activities for all ages, the market offers residents an opportunity to slow down and spend a few hours enjoying the bazaar..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..A treasure hunt for homegrown brandsFor shoppers, a walk through The Ripe Market offers the chance to discover products beyond the usual retail shelves. Independent businesses showcase everything from fashion, jewellery, and accessories to homeware, artwork, beauty products, and handcrafted gifts.Among the returning participants is Hasabi Organic Farm Al Ain, which brings locally grown organic vegetables to the market..“These are all local and organic vegetables from our farm. Every day, they are freshly harvested,” Riyad Hossin, a salesman at the farm, told Gulf News.“We have been participating for 12 years now, and it really helps because customers are coming.”.Further along, shoppers can discover Birs Atelier, where handbags are handmade using recycled materials, with customised designs and individual stitching.“We create handmade handbags with customised designs. We use recycled materials, and we do everything ourselves, every stitch by hand,” shared owner Birsan Kan.“We have different sizes and price points. You can find a piece of your childhood in every design, and everything is locally made here in the UAE.”.Kan has noted that her participation in the market has helped her business grow, prompting her to take a more permanent presence this season.“This is my second year participating in The Ripe Market, and this time I have decided to have a permanent place because it helps my business grow. The Ripe Market has a lot of footfall and marketing around brands, and I want to be part of it.”.Upcycled wood turns into a speakerFor those interested in sustainable products, Mango Beat demonstrates an unusual take on the smartphone speaker, giving discarded material a new purpose.“The idea is to create a speaker and amplifier for smartphones without using wires, batteries, or electricity. It is one piece of wood, and it is upcycled,” explained Charles Jabbour, a partner at Mango Beat.“We buy used wood and upcycle it into something completely handmade.”.Jabbour has bared that the larger speakers can amplify sound by up to seven times, while the smaller ones can amplify it by up to five times.The business also works with farming communities in Thailand to repurpose waste wood and turn it into products for international markets.Jabbour has participated at the Academy Park location for about eight years and highlighted that the market offers a valuable opportunity to connect with people interested in sustainability.“It is a great place to connect with the community. You have a lot of people here who are professionals and work in ESG (environmental, social, and governance) and sustainability.” He added, “It is great to introduce our product, which resonates with a lot of people and is not something you find in many places.”.Follow the sweet treatsShopping is only part of the experience. The market also brings together food concepts serving breakfast, coffee, street food, sweet treats, and family-friendly favourites.Visitors can begin their morning with a coffee and breakfast, stop for a meal between shopping trips, or pick up something sweet while exploring the stalls.The variety of food and drink options makes it easy to turn a short visit into a longer outing, whether meeting friends, supporting a local food business, or taking a break from the activities..For Tatiano Kamoeva, a marketing director who visited the market, the appeal extends beyond shopping.“Padel brought me here, but I also love crafted things and everything that is handmade. I love the handmade plates, some drinks and food,” exclaimed Kamoev.“You can get a lot of entertainment and cultural things. It is a great place.”.Visitor Elle McCabe, an operations manager, has mentioned that she came to support a friend who has a fine-dining booth at the market.“My friend has a fine-dining booth, and I came to see and support them. This place is absolutely fab. The baby shops are also really cute,” described McCab..Keeping children busyFor families, The Ripe Market offers more than shopping and food. Children can look forward to activities including a petting zoo, pony rides, arts and crafts, workshops, inflatables, mini train rides, and a carousel.The range of attractions gives younger visitors plenty to explore, whether they want to spend time with animals, get creative at a workshop, or enjoy the rides. Parents can browse the stalls or stop for a meal while making time for activities that appeal to the whole family.The market's stage will also host family-friendly entertainment throughout the season, including magic shows, music, and themed performances..For Emma Pilal, who attended the opening with her son Danis, the magic show was a highlight of their visit.“I came here for the magic show, and we really enjoyed it. We will definitely come back to explore the other shops and activities,” remarked Pilal.The market's open-air setting allows families to move between the attractions, shopping stalls, and food outlets, making it possible to enjoy several experiences during one visit..Dubai Police bring community activities to the marketDubai Police will once again take part in the market's community programme, with activities planned throughout the season.Visitors can look forward to performances by the Dubai Police Marching Band, K9 demonstrations, and displays of Dubai Police supercars. Children will also have opportunities to participate in activities, alongside appearances by officer Amna and captain Mansour.The programme adds another attraction for families and gives younger visitors opportunities to engage with Dubai Police in a community setting..Live performances add to the weekend atmosphereBeyond the shopping stalls and food counters, live entertainment will feature throughout the season, with music, themed musical acts, magic shows, and family-friendly performances planned.Homegrown performers will be part of the programme, offering visitors a chance to pause between activities, gather around the stage, and enjoy live acts in an informal outdoor setting.The entertainment schedule will change throughout the season, giving regular visitors different performances and activities to discover on return visits..Make room for wellness and sportThose looking to do more than shop and eat can also explore the market's wellness and sports offering.Free sessions will include yoga, Pilates, sound healing, and mindfulness, giving visitors opportunities to stretch, unwind, or take a break from the pace of everyday life.Sports activities planned throughout the season will include swimming, padel, tennis, horse riding, football, rugby, and gymnastics.The mix of activities is designed to appeal to different ages and interests, making the market an option for visitors who want to combine a social outing with an active weekend..15 years of bringing communities togetherAs The Ripe Market enters its 15th year, its story goes beyond the products on its stalls. It is also about the small businesses that have found customers, the makers who have shared their craft, and the families and friends who have returned to spend their weekends together.For vendors such as Al Ain Hasabi Organic Farm and Mango Beat, years of participation have helped build connections with customers and the wider community. For businesses such as Birs Atelier, the market offers a platform to grow, while visitors come for everything from handmade finds and food to entertainment and time with family..In a city as diverse as Dubai, The Ripe Market brings these different experiences together in one place, creating opportunities for people to discover local talent, support independent businesses, and connect with others.As another season begins, the market’s 15-year milestone is a reminder that its lasting appeal lies not just in what visitors take home, but in the people they meet and the community they become part of.The Ripe Market runs every Saturday and Sunday from 9am to 9pm at Dubai Police Academy Park in Umm Suqeim until May 2 next year..The Ripe Market is back: What to expect at Dubai Police Academy Park this season.Inside Abu Dhabi Mall’s Ripe Market, where local creativity takes centre stage.What the Khorfakkan Mango Festival offers to local farmers and families.Hatta Farming Festival 2026: 7 rare finds you can buy from Emirati farmers at the local market

It is one piece of wood, and it is upcycled,” explained Charles Jabbour, a partner at Mango Beat.“We buy used wood and upcycle it into something completely handmade.”.Jabbour has bared that the larger speakers can amplify sound by up to seven times, while the smaller ones can amplify it by up to five times.The business also works with farming communities in Thailand to repurpose waste wood and turn it into products for international markets.Jabbour has participated at the Academy Park location for about eight years and highlighted that the market offers a valuable opportunity to connect with people interested in sustainability.“It is a great place to connect with the community.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Police recognised at global summit in Seoul for project management excellence
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Police has received international recognition from the Project Management Institute (PMI) for its excellence in planning, managing and delivering projects and initiatives in line with global professional standards.The recognition was announced during the PMI Global Summit Series Seoul, the Republic of Korea, which brought together project management leaders, experts and specialists from around the world.The achievement recognises the work of the Initiatives and Projects Department within Dubai Police’s General Department of Excellence and Pioneering and highlights the force’s approach to turning strategic plans into practical projects with measurable results.Dubai Police has developed an integrated project management system built around effective planning, good governance and measuring performance and impact. The system helps ensure that initiatives are delivered efficiently, resources are managed effectively, and projects contribute to the force’s wider strategic objectives.Major General Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah Rashid Al Mualla, Director of the General Department of Excellence and Pioneering at Dubai Police, said the recognition reflects Dubai Police’s forward-looking approach to project management, enabling the organisation to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans and meaningful, sustainable outcomes.“This recognition from the Project Management Institute, one of the world’s leading professional organisations in the field, reflects the maturity of Dubai Police’s institutional practices and the capabilities of its personnel in managing projects through governance, flexibility, impact measurement and future foresight,” he said.

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan bin Mohammed names RTA winner of Dubai-it Award for Institutions in the Field of Government
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 11th October, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, congratulated the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) in Dubai on winning the ‘Dubai-it Award’ for Institutions in the Field of Government.The award recognises RTA’s tangible results in accelerating services, improving operational efficiency, and enhancing customer experience across the roads and transport sectors, as well as its adoption of the ‘Dubai-it’ philosophy as an institutional culture and work approach.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan stated, “We announced the Dubai-it Award to celebrate Dubai’s philosophy of work, brought to life by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai. Dubai-it means achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time.”Sheikh Hamdan added, “Today, RTA receives the award for Institutions in the Field of Government. It delivers major roads, bridges and tunnels at 2x global benchmarks for speed and efficiency without compromising quality. Metro punctuality stands at 99.7 percent as the network continues to expand with more stations. Autonomous mobility and high-quality cycling routes advance at pace. Anticipating the city’s needs. Enabling Dubai’s next phase of growth. This is how RTA does Dubai-it. Congratulations to the team.”The Roads and Transport Authority won the award for adopting the ‘Dubai-it’ philosophy as an institutional culture and work approach based on delivering exceptional projects in record time and achieving tangible, high-quality results that reinforce Dubai's status as a global benchmark in mobility, infrastructure, and government services.The Authority embodied the Dubai-it philosophy by executing major road, bridge, and tunnel projects at double the global speed and efficiency rates, including iconic projects such as the Infinity Bridge. It maintained the highest average pace of delivery across bridges, tunnels and infrastructure projects, equivalent to double the global completion speed, at a cost below the global average, while ensuring superior quality.The Authority achieved a Dubai Metro punctuality rate of 99.7 percent, alongside the continuous expansion of the metro network and station upgrades. It developed systems to monitor and address road feedback in under 24 hours and accelerated dozens of driver and vehicle-related services, making them among the fastest globally.Furthermore, RTA executed a series of road projects and over 250 traffic improvements that contributed to cutting travel times by up to 60 percent. It developed and operated AI-powered autonomous taxis to support the future of mobility in Dubai, developed the Air Taxi Station in Dubai to add a new mode to the city's future mobility ecosystem, and expanded and improved cycle tracks with high quality and in record time.Additionally, RTA implemented 117 quick-win improvements within two years and succeeded in providing 82 services without any waiting time, reflecting its focus on reducing completion times and responding faster to the needs of transport network users.These accomplishments reflect Dubai’s philosophy of work, ‘Dubai-it’: achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time.Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Chairman of the Executive Office of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, said, “The Dubai-it Award received hundreds of nominations reflecting great diversity in initiatives, projects, and achievements that embody Dubai’s work philosophy. They demonstrate the ability of individuals and institutions to turn ambitions into tangible results. RTA's approach clearly reflected this philosophy on the ground by combining quality, speed, and continuity, turning challenges into opportunities for development and service improvement.”He said, “RTA’s recognition with the Dubai-it Award for Institutions in the Field of Government highlights an institutional model built on sustained achievement, rapid responsiveness, precision in execution, and tangible impact on society. It embodies Dubai-it: achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time, creating lasting impact that strengthens Dubai’s competitiveness and quality of life.”Al Gergawi added, “The award sheds light on the Authority's efforts in converting feedback into measurable improvements, its commitment to innovation to simplify procedures and advance services, and its implementation of continuous improvements to boost efficiency and elevate the customer experience in Dubai.”His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, launched the Dubai-it initiative to advance the philosophy of work behind Dubai’s transformation: bold ambition, excellent execution, and the determination to make the extraordinary happen.The initiative aims to embed this philosophy across institutions and companies, making it a shared culture and an enduring way of working. To see beyond what exists. To act with speed and the highest standards. To create lasting value for the city and its people, with every achievement opening the way for the next.Under the directives of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the Dubai-it Award was launched to honour the individuals, projects, companies, and institutions that bring this philosophy to life. An annual recognition of bold ambition, excellence in execution, and lasting impact. By celebrating those who turn possibility into achievement, the award sets the pace for Dubai’s future development goals.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai doubles Oraseya Capital fund to AED1 billion to accelerate AI, fintech and future-tech investment
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority (DIEZ) has doubled the size of the venture capital fund managed by its investment arm, Oraseya Capital, from AED500 million to AED1 billion, strengthening its capacity to support high-potential companies and reinforcing Dubai's position as a global hub for venture capital, innovation and future industries. The expansion is designed to increase support for technology companies with global growth potential while advancing the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33. His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of DIEZ, said: "Doubling the size of the Oraseya Capital fund reflects our confidence in Dubai's position as a hub for technology leaders and translates the directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, to build a diversified, knowledge-based economy driven by innovation." He added: "Expanding the fund's capacity strengthens the ecosystem around promising companies, providing them with the capital, expertise and opportunities they need to grow from Dubai into regional and global markets." "We have strong confidence in Dubai's future as a global centre for capital and innovation. Our role is to translate this confidence into tangible investments, companies and economic opportunities that contribute to the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33, strengthen Dubai's competitiveness, and reinforce the UAE's position as a global hub for the new economy and investment in future-focused sectors," Sheikh Ahmed said. DIEZ has also increased Oraseya Capital's maximum investment per company from USD3 million to USD6 million, equivalent to approximately AED22 million, enabling the fund to participate in larger funding rounds and support companies at more advanced stages of growth. The fund's investment scope will expand beyond companies directly linked to the UAE to include global businesses of strategic relevance to the country, opening access to a wider range of opportunities across international markets. Under the expanded mandate, Oraseya Capital will support founders at every stage of growth, including companies beyond Series B funding rounds. The move will allow the fund to back businesses with proven models and demonstrated growth potential while continuing to support early-stage start-ups. DIEZ said the strategy is aimed at helping build the next generation of billion-dollar unicorn companies, strengthening Dubai's position as a global business hub and a launchpad for regional and international expansion. Strong track record Oraseya Capital has established itself as one of the region's most active venture capital investors since its launch. According to venture capital data platform MAGNiTT, the fund has ranked as the UAE's most active investor by number of deals for three consecutive years. It ranked first in the UAE in 2024 and retained the position in 2025. In MAGNiTT's first-half 2026 rankings, it remained the UAE's most active investor by both overall deal count and early-stage investment activity, while placing second across the Middle East and North Africa in both categories. The fund was also named Venture Capital Firm of the Year at the Entrepreneur Middle East Awards 2025. His Excellency Dr Mohammed Al Zarooni, Executive Chairman of DIEZ. His Excellency Dr Mohammed Al Zarooni, Executive Chairman of DIEZ, said: "Doubling the size of the fund reflects the strength of Oraseya Capital's model and the results it has achieved since its launch. "It enhances our capacity to respond to the ambitions and needs of promising companies at different stages of growth, while creating opportunities for more impactful investment partnerships. "We are taking Oraseya Capital into a new phase of growth and expansion guided by a clear investment approach that brings together capital, expertise, guidance and access to an integrated network of investors and partners," he added. Dr Al Zarooni said DIEZ's ambition extends beyond investing in start-ups to supporting companies capable of competing on the global stage, with Dubai serving as their base for expansion. source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment (MBRHE) has announced the launch of a dedicated service area for "Generation Shapers", becoming the first government entity in Dubai to introduce the initiative. The move is aimed at enhancing customer experience and recognising the role of mothers in raising future generations and strengthening families and society. The dedicated area has been designed to provide a comfortable and convenient service experience by addressing the needs of customers classified as "Generation Shapers" and facilitating their access to MBRHE services. MBRHE said the initiative translates its appreciation of "Generation Shapers" into a practical institutional initiative, recognising their contribution to raising children, instilling values and supporting the development of a cohesive society. The initiative also aligns with the objectives of the UAE's Year of the Family 2026, which seeks to strengthen family bonds and reinforce the family as the foundation of society and a driver of development. MBRHE said it remains committed to developing people-centred government services that combine quality with responsiveness to the needs of different segments of society, supporting its vision of providing an integrated housing system that enhances quality of life and promotes family and social stability in Dubai. The initiative builds on MBRHE's broader efforts in institutional excellence. In March 2026, the establishment obtained international accreditation under the International Employee Happiness and Wellbeing Standard (IEHWS) and the International Digital Customer Experience Standard (IDCXS), achieving an evaluation score of 100 per cent in both standards. MBRHE said the accreditation reflects its commitment to applying international standards to improve the work environment, enhance customer experience and support continuous improvement in the delivery of housing services.

source_snapshot.title: 11 Dubai-based companies pledge to integrate Agentic AI into their operations
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 12th October, 2026 (WAM) -- In the presence of H.H. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, a total of 11 Dubai-based companies representing diverse sectors have pledged to integrate Agentic AI technologies into their operations, with the support of Dubai Chambers.The pledge reflects the private sector's commitment to advancing the adoption of Agentic AI under Dubai's private sector Agentic AI transformation programme, launched in May this year by H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Executive Council of Dubai. Overseen by Dubai Chambers, the programme aims to enable businesses to harness the potential of these advanced technologies.The 11 companies that signed the pledge launched by Dubai Chambers are Emirates, DP World, AW Rostamani Group, Al Ansari Exchange, Dubai Islamic Bank, Kitopi, Dutco Group, Aster DM Healthcare, Innovo, Independent Food Company and HSA Group.Mohammad Ali Rashed Lootah, President and CEO of Dubai Chambers, said: “Agentic AI represents a new phase in the evolution of business models, offering significant opportunities for companies to transform their operations, improve service quality and make faster, more informed decisions. These capabilities can drive greater operational efficiency, productivity and innovation. Agentic AI also provides businesses with a strategic tool to support growth, adapt to rapid changes in the global business environment, turn challenges into opportunities for expansion and create sustainable value.”He added: “The pledge reflects growing recognition among businesses that Agentic AI is no longer a technology of the future, but an essential driver of efficiency, innovation and competitiveness. Its adoption will also enable companies to develop more agile operating models that can respond effectively to evolving business needs.”The pledge marks a practical step towards enabling companies to move beyond exploring the potential of Agentic AI to adopting intelligent solutions across their operations, including service development, internal processes and decision-making. The aim is to enhance productivity and operational efficiency while encouraging investment in technologies that support long-term growth and enable businesses to respond to rapidly changing market conditions.The participation of companies from diverse sectors reflects growing interest in adopting advanced technologies and reinforces collaboration between Dubai Chambers and the private sector to accelerate digital transformation. The initiative also contributes to developing a more innovative business environment that harnesses technology to create new economic opportunities and strengthen Dubai's global competitiveness.Dubai's private sector Agentic AI transformation programme, includes specialised training tracks recently launched by Dubai Chambers to support the adoption of these technologies. The training aims to equip more than 14,000 companies represented within Dubai Chamber of Commerce's Business Groups and Business Councils with the knowledge and capabilities needed to integrate Agentic AI into their administrative and operational activities.The programme also includes the establishment of specialised incubators for Agentic AI companies, alongside initiatives to support the development and adoption of Agentic AI solutions. Other areas of focus include developing young talent, expanding access to funding, facilitating knowledge sharing and strengthening capabilities across Dubai’s business community.

source_snapshot.title: AquaIndex plans to launch UAE water token as part of global expansion
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 12th October, 2026 (WAM) -- AquaIndex, a water asset management and pricing company, has announced plans to launch a dedicated regional water token for the UAE as part of its strategy to expand globally and build a digital infrastructure for the documentation, pricing, ownership management and trading of water reserves using real-world asset (RWA) tokenisation technology.Ahmed Bin Sulayem, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, DMCC, said, "When we signed our partnership with AquaIndex in 2025, our ambition was clear: to support the launch of what we believe is the world's first digital asset token backed directly by freshwater resources, to help develop a more transparent global marketplace for water, and to establish Dubai as a leading centre for this emerging sector." He added that Dubai remains a natural platform for the company's next phase of international growth. Through DMCC's ecosystem connecting trade, logistics, technology and finance, the partnership aims to bring physical assets into blockchain-powered markets and support better stewardship of water resources.AquaIndex expects its enterprise platform to go live in Q4 2026. The platform is designed to create standardised digital representations of certified physical water reserves, enabling the underlying assets to be documented, tracked and managed. It also incorporates an automated physical redemption and logistics engine, connecting smart-contract execution with physical delivery at certified reservoir and distribution locations. This is designed to enable holders of water tokens to redeem their allocation for physical water through established delivery infrastructure.The company's initial physical tokens are backed by water sourced from a regulated aquifer in the USA. The initial asset base proposed for tokenisation comprises up to 11 billion barrels of water, with an estimated value of approximately US$5 billion. The associated delivery network includes more than 20 miles of existing pipeline infrastructure, with individual pipelines offering potential physical delivery capacity of approximately 300,000 barrels per day at large scale.Yaacov Shirazi, Chairman and Founder of AquaIndex, said the company is building the technology layer that can connect the physical resource with transparent pricing, verified ownership and efficient delivery. He emphasised that the UAE, with its global commodities ecosystem and increasingly sophisticated digital infrastructure, is an important part of the company's global expansion strategy. Shirazi added, "We are not simply digitising an asset. We are building the infrastructure that connects the digital representation of water to the physical resource itself from verification and documentation through to redemption and delivery."AquaIndex is also developing its infrastructure on the Canton Network, including the operation of a dedicated Canton Network Validator Node to support data privacy and secure transactions. The company is simultaneously deploying its core smart-contract infrastructure on Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) architecture, supporting interoperability with wider digital technologies and automated logistics systems. It expects initial commodity allocations and secondary-market integrations to go live by the end of 2026, with further international reserve assets and commercial applications planned as the platform expands, alongside exploring growth opportunities across the GCC to support water security.

source_snapshot.title: 1 Billion Followers Summit opens submissions for $1 million AI Film Award 2027
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 12th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The 1 Billion Followers Summit has opened submissions for the second edition of the AI Film Award 2027, offering a $1 million grand prize to creators worldwide for AI-generated films exploring humanitarian, social and environmental issues.Organised in partnership with BytePlus, ByteDance's enterprise technology services arm, and supported this year by TikTok, the award aims to encourage innovative storytelling and expand the use of artificial intelligence in content creation.The winning film will be announced during the fifth edition of the 1 Billion Followers Summit, taking place in Dubai from 8th to 10th January 2027.Alia Al Hammadi, Vice Chairperson of the UAE Government Media Office and Deputy CEO of the 1 Billion Followers Summit, said the initiative supports the UAE's ambition to strengthen its position as a global hub for innovation, technology and the digital economy.She said, "The 1 Billion Followers Summit helps translate this vision into practical opportunities by bringing together creators, talent, technology companies, digital platforms and experts, providing a space to experiment with new ideas and transform them into stories and projects that reach the world."She added, "Through this award, we aspire to discover new talent capable of shaping the future of content creation and presenting inspiring examples that demonstrate how artificial intelligence can enhance human imagination rather than replace it."Al Hammadi said the award encourages creators to use AI responsibly and innovatively to explore new forms of expression, address societal issues and produce meaningful stories for global audiences.Long Li, General Manager for the Middle East and Africa at BytePlus, said the partnership reflects the importance of supporting creators and strengthening their connections with digital platforms and technology companies.He said, "The 1 Billion Followers Summit provides an important global platform for discovering talent and new ideas. The award combines human creativity with advanced AI capabilities, giving creators opportunities to explore new approaches to storytelling and address issues that matter to communities worldwide. We look forward to seeing the entries and the new perspectives they offer on the future of content creation in the age of AI."He added, "At BytePlus, we believe technology has the greatest impact when it gives creators more room to experiment and express themselves, helps them reach new audiences in innovative ways, and transforms their ideas into stories and visual experiences that reach a global audience."Entries will be assessed on AI integration, storytelling, creativity, aesthetics and technical execution.The competition covers five themes: Society, Community & Humanitarian Issues; Truth, Fake News & Misinformation; Humans & AI; Climate, Nature & Our Changing Planet; and Human Relationships.Applicants must be at least 18 years old and submit original films lasting five to seven minutes, in a cinematic 16:9 horizontal format, at 1080p resolution, as MOV or MP4 files. Films may be produced in any language but must include English subtitles. Creators retain ownership and copyright of their work.At least 70 percent of each finished film must be generated using ByteDance's Dreamina Seedance AI video-generation technology. Other AI tools, conventional editing techniques and original live-action footage may be used for supporting elements, provided the minimum Seedance requirement is met.Submissions will remain open until 20th November 2026, with the top 10 shortlisted films announced and public voting opening on 15th December, followed by the unveiling of the five finalists on 25th December. The finalists will be screened in Dubai, and the winner of the $1 million grand prize will be announced during the fifth edition of the 1 Billion Followers Summit, taking place from 8th to 10th January 2027.

importance of supporting creators and strengthening their connections with digital platforms and technology companies.He said, "The 1 Billion Followers Summit provides an important global platform for discovering talent and new ideas.

source_snapshot.title: Will your Dubai school hike fees next year? How KHDA's 24-hour inspections and ratings come into play
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai parents were relieved when school fees were frozen for the 2026-27 academic year. With the Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) bringing back school inspections, the big question now is whether your child's school will be allowed to raise fees next year since a school's inspection rating can influence its eligibility for an increase, if one is approved.Gulf News explains KHDA’s new model of inspection visits, when inspections will start, how ratings could affect eligibility, how appeals work and what will drive the final decision.Why is KHDA changing its inspections?According to KHDA, inspections are returning after a two-year pause. KHDA Director-General Aisha Miran said teachers and schools had asked for fewer inspections, so they had time to make improvements.Hence, after 17 years of annual inspections, she pushed for a pause, and KHDA now wants to see whether schools used that time well.What are QA 1 and QA 2?They are the new types of inspection visits named Quality Assurance 1 and Quality Assurance 2 visits.According to KHDA, QA 1 is a full, conventional inspection of the entire school against the 2015 UAE School Inspection Framework. A school’s overall rating could improve, decline or remain unchanged following the inspection.If a fee increase is approved, the school’s eligibility for an increase will be determined by its updated inspection rating.QA 2 is a targeted visit for schools where data indicates specific areas for improvement, but where a full inspection is not expected to change the school’s overall rating. KHDA will focus on those areas, offering advice and support to help schools improve.A QA 2 visit will not change a school’s existing rating. Therefore, if a fee increase is approved, schools undergoing QA 2 will have their eligibility for any increase assessed based on their existing inspection ratings from two years ago, in accordance with the applicable fee framework.Which schools will surely undergo QA1?Schools entering their third year of operation will undergo a comprehensive quality assurance visit covering overall performance, teaching standards, and learning outcomes.The assessment will conclude with a detailed report and an overall school rating.Why not inspect every school fully?According to KHDA, it wants to use its time and resources where they can make a difference. It will use school data, including learning outcomes, parental complaints and leadership evaluation, to decide who gets which visit.KHDA says artificial intelligence will support this, with human oversight. KHDA does not want to reassess schools that are already performing well.What are the new focus areas in inspections?KHDA will place additional emphasis on four areas: early childhood education, the quality of education for Emirati students, inclusive education for students of determination, and Arabic language teaching and learning.These priorities complement the existing UAE School Inspection Framework.Why only 24 hours' notice?Schools will get no more than 24 hours' notice. According to KHDA, the aim is for schools to maintain standards all year rather than preparing for a known inspection date. Miran said parents have told KHDA that schools can look very different when inspectors are expected. KHDA wants inspectors to see everyday teaching and interactions, and to have more confidence in the results.Will schools know which category they are in?Not in advance. According to KHDA, schools will find out whether they have QA 1 or QA 2 only 24 hours before the visit.Miran said KHDA has some initial indications, but the final decision will use the latest data.There is one exception. According to KHDA, any school entering its third year of operation will undergo a QA 1 inspection, as it is still considered new. Meanwhile, schools in their first or second year will get specialised visits instead.How could QA 1/QA 2 affect a fee increase?According to KHDA, fee increases are linked to a school's most recent inspection result. Some schools will have a rating from this academic year, while others will keep one from up to two years ago.A QA 2 school keeps its existing rating. For example, a school rated Very Good stays Very Good.For a QA 1 school, the new rating, whether higher, lower or unchanged, is what counts. Neither type of visit guarantees an increase.How are Dubai schools rated?KHDA rates private schools using the UAE School Inspection Framework.This assesses six areas: students’ achievement; students’ personal and social development and innovation skills; teaching and assessment; curriculum; protection, care, guidance and support; and leadership and management.What are the six school rating categories?Schools receive one of six overall ratings: Outstanding, Very Good, Good, Acceptable, Weak or Very Weak.Good is the standard expected of schools, while Acceptable represents the minimum quality level required.Currently there are no Very Weak schools in Dubai as per the latest inspection results.When will new inspections begin?According to KHDA, it will collect updated data from schools in October.This will cover student attainment, leadership, training, and learning and development.Miran said inspections can begin any time after the authority receives all the relevant data.No exact start date has been given but it can start any time after the authority compiles the data in October.How can schools appeal?Once an inspection is complete, the rating is shared with the school. KHDA said there is a provision for schools to appeal an inspection rating.According to Miran, the appeal period is two months, followed by one month for KHDA to review it and decide whether to uphold or change the rating.The report is then finalised. Results are usually announced together at the end of the first inspection cycle, though KHDA could look at other options if timing matters.How do the ECI and fee framework work?The Education Cost Index (ECI) reflects the cost of running a school, including staff wages, support services and rent.According to KHDA, it is typically calculated in April. It was set at 2.6 per cent in 2024 and 2.35 per cent for 2025-26, announced on May 2, 2025. As a simple illustration, a 2.35 per cent rise on annual fees of Dh50,000 would be Dh1,175, against Dh1,300 at 2.6 per cent.The fee framework decides how far a school can go, based on its rating. In previous years, schools that kept their rating could raise fees by up to the ECI.Schools that improved their rating could qualify for higher multipliers, up to twice the ECI depending on the rating jump. Schools whose rating fell could not raise fees.What is still unknown?According to KHDA, it is not yet clear whether the same formula will apply next year, or whether the ECI or framework will change.Under an earlier arrangement, when inspections were paused, schools were allowed to raise fees only by a set percentage rather than under the framework. It largely depended on the school's rating and the ECI.That is why KHDA stresses that the mechanism for next year is not yet known.Who decides whether fees will rise?The final decision rests with Dubai's leadership. KHDA confirmed on May 22, 2026, that private school fees will stay unchanged for 2026-27, under the guidance of Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai and Chairman of The Executive Council.The freeze came with a Dh1.5 billion economic incentives package.It is not known if the government will reassess the situation or reconsider a freeze on school fees.So, a good rating does not mean fees will rise. Any increase will finally depend on the fee framework, the ECI and a government decision, and the new inspection system does not, on its own, confirm one. The decision is expected in April or May.What should parents take away?The new system decides how schools are assessed, while the possibility and size of any fee increase will depend on the framework, the ECI and a government decision..KHDA to inspect Dubai schools with no more than 24 hours’ notice.Dubai announces no private school fee hike for 2026–27, KHDA confirms.What Dubai schools should prepare for KHDA’s 24-hour notice inspections.Dubai schools 2026–27: The four major rules every UAE parent needs to know

source_snapshot.title: Resolve Dubai rental disputes quickly: Amicable solutions without court
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Landlords and tenants in Dubai are increasingly resolving rental disputes without lengthy court proceedings, with 2,350 cases worth Dh401 million settled amicably in an average of just six days during the first nine months of 2026.The figures, released by Dubai’s Rental Disputes Centre (RDC), highlight the growing importance of conciliation as a faster and less confrontational way to settle disagreements between property owners and tenants.Between January and September 2026, the centre successfully concluded 2,350 amicable settlement cases, helping disputing parties reach mutually acceptable solutions while protecting their legal rights.How the settlement process workUnder the RDC’s conciliation system, landlords and tenants involved in rental disagreements are given an opportunity to resolve their differences through a structured legal process.Rather than proceeding directly to formal litigation, both parties can negotiate a mutually acceptable agreement with the assistance of the centre’s Conciliation and Settlement Department.Once an agreement is reached, it is approved by a supervising judge, giving it the legal force of an enforceable instrument.This means the settlement is not merely an informal understanding but a legally enforceable agreement designed to protect the rights of both parties.Greater confidenceJudge Abdulqader Mousa Mohammed, Chairman of the Rental Disputes Centre, said the results demonstrated the effectiveness of Dubai’s approach to resolving rental disagreements.“The performance of the amicable settlement mechanism during the first nine months of this year underscores its capacity to bring rental disputes to swift and effective conclusions and confirms that timely resolution, procedural quality, and the protection of rights are all integral outcomes of efforts grounded in specialised expertise and an immediate response to the needs of disputing parties. The RDC continues to advance its legal framework to support the stability of contractual relationships and foster confidence in Dubai’s judicial system.”Why amicable settlements matterFor landlords and tenants, amicable settlements offer an opportunity to resolve disputes without the time and uncertainty often associated with formal court proceedings.The process allows both sides to negotiate practical solutions while preserving contractual relationships wherever possible.According to the RDC, the approach also helps reduce the social and economic consequences of prolonged rental disagreements.As Dubai’s rental market continues to grow, the centre said it remains focused on improving dispute resolution procedures, ensuring fair access to justice and encouraging landlords and tenants to settle disagreements through conciliation. .Dubai rental dispute process: How to file a case, fees, documents and what happens next.Ajman issues new decree setting fees and deposits for rental dispute cases.Dubai landlord refusing to return your security deposit? source_snapshot.title: Dubai Maritime Authority launches regulatory initiative to boost leisure anchoring practices and navigational safety
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 13th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Maritime Authority (DMA), part of the Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation (PCFC), has announced the launch of a new regulatory initiative to update, standardise and organise the guidelines governing leisure anchoring and the use of recreational mooring buoys in the waters of the Emirate of Dubai. The initiative forms part of the Authority's ongoing efforts to strengthen navigational safety, establish a clear regulatory environment and support the sustainable growth of the emirate's recreational marine sector.Sheikh Dr. Saeed bin Ahmed bin Khalifa Al Maktoum, CEO of the Dubai Maritime Authority, said: “This initiative strengthens navigational safety and ensures the orderly use of leisure anchoring areas and recreational mooring buoys in Dubai waters. It supports the sustainable growth of recreational maritime activities and ensures that regulations and guidance are clear to all stakeholders, underlining Dubai's commitment to consolidating its position as a global hub for safe and well-regulated marine activities.”The initiative includes the announcement of Circular No. (35) of 2026 Regarding the Guidelines for Leisure Anchorage and Recreational Mooring Buoys in Dubai Waters, ahead of its implementation. The circular will help raise safety standards, improve regulatory efficiency and provide a clear, unified framework for all parties involved in recreational marine activities, including owners of marine craft, operators and their agents, marinas and marine service providers. It is designed to ensure safe and orderly anchoring practices that comply with safety and marine environmental protection requirements, and to support the sustainability of the vital sector.The Dubai Maritime Authority affirmed that the step forms part of the Authority's strategic vision to develop the maritime ecosystem and strengthen Dubai's standing as a leading global destination for recreational maritime activities by applying regulatory best practice and working in close integration with its partners in the government and private sectors. The circular and its accompanying guidelines will be applied in accordance with authorised provisions and procedures, and in coordination with all relevant entities and parties.The Authority is monitoring the implementation of all regulatory measures to ensure full compliance with the rules and guidelines. This includes adherence to anchoring requirements; observance of navigational safety requirements, including the regulations for preventing collisions at sea and the principles of good seamanship; and protection of the marine environment and the prevention of any harmful practices. He also stressed the need to report incidents and emergencies immediately so that they can be dealt with quickly and efficiently.Dubai Maritime Authority emphasised that compliance with the initiative and its accompanying guidelines is a shared responsibility of everyone venturing out to sea. It promotes a safe and sustainable marine environment and helps consolidate Dubai's position as a leading global destination for recreational marine activities, combining safety, efficiency and excellence in service delivery.

to Jumeirah Golf Estates Metro Station opens, according to an announcement shared on Etihad Rail’s official Instagram account.The opening marks a significant improvement in public transport connectivity for Etihad Rail passengers, who will be able to travel between the train and Metro stations on foot instead of relying on taxis or buses for the transfer..Direct connection to Dubai MetroThe approximately 400-metre pedestrian bridge will link Etihad Rail's Al Yalayis station with Jumeirah Golf Estates Metro Station on the Dubai Metro Red Line.For passengers arriving in Dubai by train, the connection will provide access to the wider Metro network, including key commercial, residential and tourist destinations across the city.Similarly, commuters travelling from other parts of Dubai will be able to take the Metro to Jumeirah Golf Estates and walk to the Etihad Rail station to board their trains.The new link is particularly useful for passengers travelling without a private vehicle, removing the need for a separate road transfer between the two stations..More options for Etihad Rail passengersEtihad Rail launched its passenger services on September 30, connecting Dubai's communities, including Dubai Production City and Dubai Sports City.The opening of the pedestrian bridge adds a direct walking connection between the two transport networks.Passengers can also purchase source_snapshot.title: UAE orders recall of face mask batch over possible contamination
source_snapshot.text: The UAE has ordered a recall of a batch of face masks because of concerns about possible contamination of the material used in its manufacture. The Emirates Drug Establishment issued the recall for Nin 160 FMB-NML Facemask C G blue, batch number 20251015. It is described as blue in colour and three-ply in structure. The Dubai Health Authority also issued a circular on Monday instructing healthcare centres to comply with the recall. Officials said Ningbo ETDZ Holdings Ltd in China manufactured the masks, and Globemed Care LLC distributed them in the UAE. The drug regulator said the recall was ordered after a quality complaint. Inspections identified foreign material or contamination in units from the affected batch. Healthcare professionals, hospitals and clinics and pharmacies must immediately stop selling, supplying, distributing or using the affected batch. They must identify and quarantine all available stock, then arrange for its return to the local supplier or distributor, Globemed Care LLC. They must also maintain records of quantities identified, quarantined, and returned. Residents who purchased the affected product should stop using any packs with batch number 20251015 and return them to the point of purchase or supplier. Healthcare providers must report any product quality complaints or adverse incidents related to the masks through EDE-approved reporting channels. Globemed Care LLC has also been ordered to retrieve all distributed quantities from the UAE market. It must also provide the regulator with details of quantities imported, distributed, returned, and remaining in stock, as well as a complete UAE distribution list. The regulator also urged people to report any quality concerns or adverse incidents involving the product directly to the authority.

source_snapshot.title: Spices, shipwrecks and ancient trade routes: Louvre Abu Dhabi explores 1,000 years of Indian Ocean history
source_snapshot.text: Visitors to Louvre Abu Dhabi's latest exhibition begin their journey in darkness, lights above mimicking a star-filled sky. It's a reminder of a time when sailors relied on the heavens to navigate the Indian Ocean, carrying spices, precious stones and textiles between distant civilisations. Such voyages connected communities from East Africa and the Arabian Peninsula to India, China and South-East Asia, establishing commercial and cultural relationships that developed over centuries. Their history is explored in Spices and Wonders: Sailing the Indian Ocean, opening at Louvre Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, October 14, and running until February 14, 2027. Organised in partnership with the Guimet National Museum of Asian Arts in Paris, the exhibition brings together about 240 artworks and historical objects from 24 lenders, covering maritime exchange from antiquity to the 17th century. Among them are archaeological discoveries, jewellery, religious artefacts and objects recovered from shipwrecks. Six detailed models of historic vessels and specially created maps illustrate how sailors crossed vast waters and transported goods between continents. The exhibition places the Arabian Gulf at the centre of its narrative, examining the region's historical role in these networks. “The story is told from here, and that is something we consider very important at Louvre Abu Dhabi: telling the story from the region,” says Guilhem Andre, the museum's director of scientific, curatorial and collections management “This has never really been done on this scale before.” The exhibition features loans from institutions including the Asian Civilisations Museum in Singapore, the National Museum of the Philippines and the Al Sabah Collection in Kuwait . source_snapshot.title: Dubai's shared housing rules will lead to better quality of life for those on low incomes, says official
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's crackdown on overcrowded and illegally sub-let apartments will result in a better life for residents on low incomes, a senior official from the emirate's municipality has said. The Dubai Municipality's shared housing guide sets standards for building design, occupancy, health and safety, shared amenities and approved locations. It gives landlords until September 1, 2027, to comply with the new requirements across 43 designated areas of the emirate. Nasser Al Shaibani, structural control section manager at Dubai Municipality, said most tenants living in shared accommodation previously did not have any contracts "or any legal backbone to their residential status”. “With this law, tenants can have a one or two-month contract, which gives them the flexibility to change, to go and come back while having legal support," he said. “This will have a big impact on Dubai, as we'll see people moving to better housing and a better quality of life.” The new regulations address unregulated residential practices , prevent rooms from being subdivided, and protect the privacy and rights of owners and occupants. The new law requires buildings to be designated as either individual or family-shared housing. “Each building should be designated only for individuals or only for families; you cannot mix both permits within one building,” Mr Al Shaibani said. “Within this year, we are giving the building owners time to get the necessary approval from Dubai Municipality, Dubai Land Authority, Civil Defence and Rera. “During this time, Dubai Municipality will keep on monitoring those buildings. We will continue visiting and we will do the inspections. This period does not exempt them from unpermitted building modification." The municipality has received six applications for shared-housing permits so far. Three of them have been approved through the Build in Dubai platform. Apartment blocks designated for shared accommodation are close to public transport and workplaces to reduce commuter traffic and encourage people to walk or cycle. A 2025 Dubai workforce report by Edenred UAE found that 60 per cent of workers earned less than Dh5,000 ($1,361) a month, creating strong demand for affordable housing. While the new regulations aim to improve housing standards, industry operators caution that higher costs could make it harder to provide affordable accommodation for all. Rayan Hanna, founder and chief executive of Next House, an affordable housing platform in Dubai specialising in short-term rentals, backed the regulations but said the sector still faces challenges. “Although subdividing apartments into smaller rooms, commonly known as partitions, and operating shared rooms in residential units was prohibited, this type of accommodation has existed across Dubai for years,” Mr Hanna told The National . “A clearer legal framework for shared housing creates opportunities for experienced operators, property owners and institutional investors. “I also believe we will see stronger enforcement against illegally subdivided and overcrowded apartments in premium residential areas, with shared housing gradually moving towards designated locations.” Next House caters to professionals visiting Dubai who are looking for short to medium-term rental agreements. Under the new standards, shared accommodation must include kitchens, sanitary facilities and designated areas for dining, recreation, laundry and clothes drying. Bedrooms must be at least five square metres per person. There must be at least one toilet for every four occupants and one shower for every six people. Kitchen space must provide at least one square metre per person, and buildings must provide bicycle parking for at least 10 per cent of residents. Landlords found in breach of the regulations can be fined up to Dh500,000 ($136,147) for a first offence, with repeat offenders facing a maximum penalty of Dh1 million. Mr Hanna, who has amended his business model to comply with the latest rules, said affordability remained the biggest challenge for many people moving to Dubai for work. He said operators may need to generate about Dh2,000 to Dh3,000 per rentable room per month to make the model financially attractive for investors and property owners. “Many people relying on bed spaces simply cannot afford more than Dh700–Dh900 a month,” he said. “The new regulations introduce minimum space requirements, which are important improvements, but they also increase operating and development costs. “The real challenge is finding the balance between making housing safe and compliant, and making it attractive for investors. I don't think these regulations alone will solve Dubai's affordable housing problem, but they're certainly a step in the right direction.” Dubai is one of the world's fastest-growing cities , with its population of about 4.8 million forecast to increase to six million by 2040. The city's infrastructure is expanding alongside its population, with extensions to public transport networks and existing communities.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Health Board of Directors reviews progress on Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital, new Diabetes Center
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 15th October, 2026 (WAM) -- In a meeting chaired by H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Dubai Health, and attended by H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice Chairman of the Board, the Dubai Health Board of Directors convened to review the latest developments on two landmark projects — the Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital and the new Diabetes Center — and discuss future initiatives.Held at the Dubai Health headquarters, the meeting was also attended by Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg, His Excellency Abdulla Abdul Rahman Al Shaibani, Walid Saeed Al Awadhi, Mohammed Hassan Al Shehhi, Professor Sir Ian Andrew Greer, Dr. Amer Sharif, and Dr. Hanan Al Suwaidi.The Board commended the advances made on the Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital, including construction progress, the development of the hospital's global partnerships strategy, and the appointment of a Chair of Cancer Care.The hospital will be a landmark addition to Dubai's healthcare landscape, offering comprehensive care that meets the highest international standards, with a patient and family-centred approach that elevates the overall treatment experience.The Board also reviewed progress on the new Diabetes Center, which was approved in November 2024 and is set to open early next year. The facility will expand access to preventive care, advance treatment programmes, and promote early detection and healthier lifestyles.H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum welcomed the Board members and acknowledged their commitment to advancing strategic projects that support the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan, which aims to develop vibrant, healthy, and inclusive communities in line with the city's growth.H.H. said: "As Dubai continues to grow, developing future-ready healthcare infrastructure is essential to meeting the needs of our population, and fulfilling our leadership's vision of a sustainable, integrated health system that places people and their quality of life at the forefront of priorities.”He also expressed his appreciation for the dedication of Dubai Health's teams, and his confidence in their ability to continue raising the bar for healthcare services, reinforcing Dubai's position as a leading healthcare destination.H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum said: "We are committed to building an integrated academic health system that unites clinical care, medical education, and research, fostering a culture of innovation and knowledge. We are working to develop specialised medical talent, advance research, and translate findings into practical applications that improve diagnosis, treatment, and patient outcomes.”Dr. Raja Easa Al Gurg said: "The Hamdan Bin Rashid Cancer Hospital and the new Diabetes Center are meaningful additions to Dubai's healthcare landscape. Together, they will support early detection, advance care pathways, and improve the experience of patients and their families”.Following the meeting, H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum and H.H. Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum witnessed the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Dubai Health and the Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment (MBRHE).The agreement aims to facilitate Dubai Health employees’ access to housing services by simplifying procedures, providing direct channels for requests and inquiries, and organising awareness workshops on available services and initiatives, helping improve the employee experience.By supporting employees with their housing needs, the MoU also aims to attract and retain young national talent in Dubai's healthcare sector, providing the stability that enables them to thrive professionally and play an active role in shaping the future of health in Dubai.Mohammed Hassan Al Shehhi, CEO of MBRHE, said: “Our partnership with Dubai Health reflects our commitment to making housing services more accessible and supporting employees’ well-being and family stability. By simplifying procedures, providing direct channels for inquiries, and organising awareness workshops, we aim to make it easier for Dubai Health employees to benefit from available housing services and initiatives”.He added: “This agreement also reflects the importance of collaboration between government entities in delivering services that put people first and contribute to a better quality of life, in line with Dubai’s vision to advance public services and community well-being.”Dr. Amer Sharif, CEO of Dubai Health, said: “We are committed to building partnerships that support our employees’ well-being and family stability, while making it easier for them to access services that meet their needs. We believe in creating a motivating work environment for our people, and value our collaboration with MBRHE in making housing services more accessible and contributing to their quality of life.”

source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Employers in the UAE must report a domestic worker's absence within five days if the worker stops reporting for duty without a valid reason and their whereabouts are unknown, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) has said.The ministry clarified that employers are required to submit a report when a domestic worker leaves work without their knowledge and they are unable to establish the worker's whereabouts or contact them..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..The report, officially known as a Domestic Worker Absence from Work complaint, must be submitted through the ministry's approved service channels within five days of the worker's unexplained absence.How employers can report an absent domestic workerEmployers can submit the report through the official MoHRE website or the MOHRE UAE mobile app.They should access the ministry's domestic worker services, select the absence-from-work reporting service, complete the application with the required details and submit it for processing.The ministry's official guidance confirms that the five-day reporting requirement applies specifically to domestic workers. It differs from the rules governing private-sector employees, for whom an absence report generally applies after more than seven consecutive days.Employers can also seek guidance on the application process or follow up on requests through the ministry's customer service number: 600590000.MoHRE urged employers to consult its official website for details of the application procedures and available channels..UAE workers can report 11 types of labour violations to MOHRE.UAE fines 42 domestic worker recruitment offices over 135 labour law violations.UAE outlines four cases requiring domestic worker agencies to issue refunds.How to report unpaid salaries anonymously in the UAE

source_snapshot.title: Zayed Authority for People of Determination, Abu Dhabi Police launch Sign Language Voice platform to enhance police services for hearing-impaired people
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 15th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Abu Dhabi Police General Headquarters, in collaboration with Zayed Authority for People of Determination, affiliated with the Department of Community Development – Abu Dhabi, has launched the Sign Language Voice platform, a product of the strategic partnership between the two entities.The platform aims to enhance access to police services for deaf and hard-of-hearing people, enabling them to communicate easily and independently through a digital channel that uses sign language. The initiative contributes to faster response times, improved service quality, and an enhanced customer experience.The platform forms part of Abu Dhabi Police’s ongoing efforts to leverage innovative digital solutions to develop a more efficient and inclusive police service ecosystem, in line with the Abu Dhabi Government’s vision for smart, human-centred services. Zayed Authority for People of Determination contributed its specialised expertise in empowering deaf people, helping ensure the development of an innovative solution that addresses their needs, facilitates access to services, and enhances their independence and privacy throughout the communication process.The Sign Language Voice platform provides a direct visual communication channel with a certified sign language interpreter, enabling immediate and accurate communication between customer service employees and deaf customers. This helps reduce the time required to access interpretation services when needed, expedite transactions, improve service quality, and promote equal access to government services.The collaboration between the two entities has encompassed numerous initiatives and projects aimed at supporting and empowering People of Determination, promoting the use of sign language, exchanging expertise, developing support services, and leveraging modern technologies to remove barriers faced by deaf people. The platform is set to be rolled out across police stations in the emirate of Abu Dhabi, further facilitating access to services and enhancing the customer experience.Abdullah Abdulalee Al Humaidan, Acting Director General of Zayed Authority for People of Determination, said that the launch of the Sign Language Voice platform reflects the success of the strategic partnership between the Authority and Abu Dhabi Police General Headquarters. He noted that it demonstrates both entities’ commitment to leveraging innovation and technology to develop more inclusive government services, in line with the aspirations of the UAE’s wise leadership to empower People of Determination and enhance their quality of life.He said: “Our strategic partnership with Abu Dhabi Police General Headquarters is an institutional partnership that has contributed, over the years, to the implementation of numerous impactful initiatives and projects, with a direct positive impact on the development of services provided to People of Determination. The launch of the Sign Language Voice platform builds on this collaboration and embodies a shared vision founded on the belief that empowering People of Determination begins with removing barriers to accessing services and harnessing modern technologies to develop smart solutions that enable deaf people to communicate with police services easily, efficiently and independently.“Zayed Authority for People of Determination continues to work with its strategic partners to develop initiatives and services for different groups of People of Determination, particularly deaf people, by promoting the use of sign language, adopting innovative digital solutions, and launching impactful projects that contribute to advancing social inclusion and empowering People of Determination to participate actively across all aspects of life. These efforts align with the emirate of Abu Dhabi’s vision to build a more inclusive society and enhance quality of life.”Major General Imran Ahmed Al Mazrouei, Director of the Human Resources Sector at Abu Dhabi Police, said that the launch of the Sign Language Voice platform represents a significant addition to the police services ecosystem. He noted that it reflects Abu Dhabi Police’s commitment to fostering an inclusive institutional environment that places people at the heart of its priorities and empowers deaf People of Determination through innovative digital solutions that facilitate efficient and independent access to services and provide a more seamless and flexible experience.He explained that the success of such initiatives relies on investing in human capital and continuously developing employees’ skills and readiness to engage effectively with all members of society, alongside leveraging modern technologies, institutional partnerships, and knowledge exchange. These efforts contribute to developing services that are more flexible and responsive to diverse needs while reinforcing the principles of inclusion, equal opportunity, and accessibility.He noted that Abu Dhabi Police continues to adopt impactful and sustainable initiatives that combine the capabilities of its human resources with technological innovation, enhancing the quality of services provided, supporting quality of life, and advancing the Abu Dhabi Government’s vision for a more inclusive and sustainable society.The launch of the Sign Language Voice platform builds on a longstanding partnership between Abu Dhabi Police and Zayed Authority for People of Determination. Over the years, the collaboration has encompassed several areas, including promoting the use of sign language, developing support services, exchanging expertise, and creating innovative solutions that address the needs of People of Determination, culminating in the use of modern digital technologies to facilitate deaf people’s access to government services.

source_snapshot.title: Aldar acquires nine residential buildings in Sharjah for AED1.1 billion
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 15th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Aldar on Thursday announced an AED1.1 billion forward purchase agreement with Arada for three residential blocks comprising over 1,100 units across nine buildings in Aljada, Sharjah’s flagship mixed-use master development.The transaction marks Aldar’s first real estate investment in the emirate and expands its develop-to-hold pipeline to AED21 billion. The transaction will add more than 1,100 units to Aldar’s portfolio, with the assets to be delivered by Arada in Q4 2029.Building on the recently announced AED15 billion development partnership between Aldar and Arada, the transaction provides Aldar with access to Sharjah’s large and growing residential market through an established integrated community. The investment also broadens Aldar’s geographic exposure while adding a high-quality residential opportunity with attractive long-term fundamentals.Talal Al Dhiyebi, Group Chief Executive Officer of Aldar, said the investment in Aljada marks the group's entry into Sharjah's residential market and expands its portfolio of rental properties, in line with its "develop-and-hold" strategy. He added that Aldar looks forward to further strengthening its partnership with Arada.Ahmed Alkhoshaibi, Group Chief Executive Officer of Arada, said: “This transaction is a strong vote of confidence in both Aljada and the Sharjah residential market more broadly. This investment marks another step in our growing partnership with Aldar, and we look forward to identifying further opportunities to work together across sectors.”Aljada is a leading mixed-use master development in Sharjah, spanning 2.2 million sqm and expected to comprise approximately 25,000 residential units at full build-out, with an anticipated gross sales value of AED35 billion.Residential handovers have been underway since 2021, with over 8,800 units delivered across multiple districts.The community is supported by completed lifestyle, hospitality, education and retail infrastructure, including the Madar family entertainment district, two international schools, two hotels, the Nest student housing complex and more than 300,000 sq ft of occupied retail space.The community is within easy reach of Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Road and Al Dhaid Road, seven minutes from Sharjah International Airport and around 20 minutes from Dubai International Airport, providing strong connectivity to both Sharjah and Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai registers 196,000 new vehicles in six months, more than 1,000 a day
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: More than 196,000 new vehicles were registered in Dubai during the first half of 2026, averaging over 1,000 a day, as population growth, urban expansion and economic activity continued to drive demand for transport services across the emirate.Dubai's Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) recorded 196,042 first-time vehicle registrations between January and June, equivalent to more than 32,000 a month..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Ahmed Mahboob, CEO of the RTA's Licensing Agency, said the sustained increase in vehicle registrations reflected Dubai's rapid population, urban and economic growth, which has led to greater demand for vehicle registration and inspection services, according to Al Bayan. He added that the authority is responding by developing an integrated service system based on advanced technologies and smart solutions to streamline procedures, speed up transactions and improve the accuracy of vehicle inspections and licensing.The RTA uses electronic data-sharing systems with relevant authorities, smart verification of vehicle and owner information, and advanced technical inspection equipment.It has also introduced updated inspection standards for electric vehicles and is incorporating artificial intelligence and machine learning into its operations.Mahboob noted that the services and initiatives available through the RTA's website and mobile application are helping accelerate procedures, improve service quality and increase customer satisfaction.Vehicle testing centres to increase to 35 by 2030Dubai currently has 30 vehicle testing centres operating across the emirate, with plans to increase the number to 35 by 2030 to accommodate growing demand.Mahboob stated that the expansion would support the emirate's continued urban and population growth while improving accessibility, operational efficiency and customer experience.The RTA also operates a centralised technical inspection system that consolidates vehicle testing data, standardises procedures and strengthens oversight across all inspection centres.The system automatically calculates inspection results, improving accuracy and supporting regulatory compliance. The authority also uses advanced technologies at its Smart Monitoring Centre alongside field inspections to strengthen supervision.Al Satwa roundabout Separately, the RTA has completed the conversion of Al Satwa roundabout into a signalised intersection, including upgrades to the surrounding road infrastructure.The project is expected to cut journey times by 50 per cent and reduce waiting times and traffic queues by up to 60 per cent during peak hours.The authority said the improvements would increase traffic efficiency on roads connecting to the intersection and improve safety for motorists and pedestrians.

source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 16th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Hamdan Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation for Medical and Educational Sciences has launched the sixth season of the Future Science Challenge, following more than a 600 percent increase in participation since its inception five years ago.Held under the theme "The Future of Roads & Mobility" and the slogan "The Smarter Road", the competition targets gifted and talented Arab students aged 10 to 17, with team registration open until 24th October 2026.The new season focuses on the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), sensors and smart systems to develop practical solutions that can make roads and mobility systems safer, smarter and more efficient.Participating teams will identify real-world challenges and source_snapshot.title: Zayed International Airport launches daily Berlin flights with Condor
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 16th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Zayed International Airport (AUH) announced on Friday the launch of Condor’s new daily, year-round service between Berlin and Abu Dhabi. The new route, operated by an Airbus A320neo, marks the first scheduled direct connection between the two capitals on Condor’s network.Condor’s codeshare partnership with Etihad Airways strengthens connectivity between Germany and Abu Dhabi by providing passengers travelling from Berlin the ability to connect to destinations across Etihad’s network, while travellers from Abu Dhabi can access Condor’s network through Berlin and beyond.The route supports the continued growth of Abu Dhabi’s tourism sector, offering visitors from Germany greater access to the emirate’s cultural and leisure attractions. It also strengthens the movement of people and supports closer commercial links between Abu Dhabi and Berlin.Carsten Nørland, Chief Commercial Officer of Abu Dhabi Airports, said the launch of Condor’s daily, year-round Berlin service strengthens direct connectivity between two dynamic, outward-looking capitals. "Through our partnership with Condor and Etihad Airways, Zayed International Airport (AUH) is connecting Abu Dhabi with Berlin and beyond, supporting greater opportunities for tourism, business and trade while reinforcing Abu Dhabi’s position as a leading global destination," he added. Haitham Ali Khamis, Acting Director of Tourism Products Development, Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi, stated, “The launch of Condor’s direct service from Berlin is an important step in expanding Abu Dhabi’s reach within the German market. Germany has consistently been a valuable source of visitors, and improved accessibility will help introduce even more travellers to the unique experiences on offer across the emirate.”Dr. Pierre Dominique Prümm, Chief Commercial Officer at Condor Airlines, said, “Together with our codeshare partner Etihad Airways, we are offering our guests not only an attractive direct service to Abu Dhabi, but also seamless connections to numerous destinations across Asia, Australia and Africa. This close cooperation brings together the strengths of both networks and gives our guests even more travel options for both leisure and business.”Lena Havia, Vice President Alliances & Joint Ventures at Etihad Airways, stated, “By bringing together our complementary networks, we are providing guests in Berlin with daily, year-round access to Abu Dhabi, as well as seamless onward connections across Etihad’s network. This is a valuable addition to what we offer in Germany, and a partnership we look forward to growing.”The route adds to Etihad's expanding presence in Germany, which already includes 35 flights a week and a Frankfurt–Abu Dhabi link, with further weekly services planned as the partnership develops.
